title: pane-wait-output-helper: typed herdr pane wait-output helper
description:
# herdr.rs: typed `pane_wait_output` helper

## Background

The docs' control-surface table lists `pane wait-output` — "Wait for text or a regular expression" — with an explicit caveat: "`pane wait-output` does not interpret agent lifecycle. It polls the selected terminal snapshot and searches it immediately, so output that already exists can match." flywheel has NO client method for it (herdr.rs: typed helpers cover workspace/pane-split/agent/worktree only, herdr.rs:301-468).

## Why (justification)

Text-level waits are the right primitive for verification phases — blocking until a test runner prints `passed|failed`, a server prints "listening", a build prints "done". Agent lifecycle waits (`agent wait`) are the right primitive for agent state; the two are complementary, and the docs are explicit that pane waits do NOT understand lifecycle. Having the typed helper is the foundation (`bd-wait-output-usage` exposes it); it also unblocks future workflow steps that need output-gated sequencing.

## Technical approach

- herdr.rs: `pane_wait_output(&mut self, pane_id: &str, mode: &str, pattern: &str, timeout_ms: Option<u64>) -> Result<PaneWaitResult>` — calls method `pane.wait_output` with params `{ target_pane_id, mode: "match"|"regex", pattern, timeout_ms }`.
- Result struct `PaneWaitResult { pane_id: String, matched_line: Option<String>, read: String }` per the docs: "`pane wait-output` returns `.result.pane_id`, `.result.matched_line`, and the matched snapshot at `.result.read`."
- Client pattern: one request per connection (herdr.rs:146-149); the wait blocks the socket — same as `agent_wait` (herdr.rs:402-413) — acceptable for a blocking primitive.
- Mode param: `"match"` (literal substring) or `"regex"` (Rust regex, herdr-side); mirror the CLI's `--match`/`--regex` distinction.

## Success criteria

- Typed helper + unit tests; wire-verified against the live server.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: request serialization (params shape, both modes, timeout present/absent); result parsing (happy path, no-match shape).
- Manual: `pane run` `sleep 2; echo done` in a scratch pane; `pane_wait_output("match", "done")` matches; a non-matching pattern with a short timeout errors (timeout), not hangs.

## Considerations

- Do NOT confuse this with `agent wait` — the helper name and doc comment must keep the lifecycle distinction explicit (the docs' caveat verbatim).
- The matched snapshot (`read`) can be large; `agent_read`-style strip-ansi/text formatting is NOT applied by pane.wait_output (raw snapshot) — parse defensively, treat as opaque string.
- No usage wiring in this bead (that is `bd-wait-output-usage`); helper + tests only.
close_reason: pane_wait_output(pane_id, mode, pattern, timeout_ms) -> Result<PaneWaitResult, HerdrError> in herdr.rs; wire-verified against live server (protocol v18). NOTE: socket method is pane.wait_for_output (NOT pane.wait_output as docs-cited); params {pane_id, source:recent, match:{type:substring|regex,value}, strip_ansi, timeout_ms}; response {type:output_matched, pane_id, matched_line, read:{text}}. Timeout path errors code 'timeout' (verified 1.5s, no hang). Pure fns wait_for_output_params + parse_wait_for_output_result with defensive parse; 6 unit tests + 1 ignored live test (PANE_ID=w13:p1 cargo test -- --ignored -> ok). 75/75 green; 6 pre-existing warnings only; dead until bd-wait-output-usage wires it (#[allow(dead_code)] noted).

title: pattern: cross-project swarm fan-out recipe
description:
# pattern-cross-project-swarm — recipe: cross-project fan-out via contact links + products

## Background

The captain's stack has 5 live herdr workspaces (chiebukuro/hachiko/dotfiles/flywheel/toron), all isolated today. Cross-project coordination (hachiko-strategist asks flywheel-orchestrator to run a backtest swarm; chiebukuro indexes toron's findings) needs `request_contact`/`products_link` (`bd-mail-cross-project-contact`). This bead ships the recipe for one project's agent triggering a swarm in another. This is ADR-0001 §9.5.

Depends on `bd-mail-cross-project-contact` (the contact/product primitives) and reuses `bd-pattern-debate-loop` (cross-project debates are the canonical high-value use).

## Recipe contract

```
# Setup (one-time, by captain/orchestrator):
ensure_product("trading-research")
products_link("trading-research", "/path/hachiko")
products_link("trading-research", "/path/flywheel")
# contact handshake (one-time):
request_contact(from=hachiko-strategist, project=hachiko, to=flywheel-orch, to_project=flywheel, reason="run backtest swarms")
# flywheel-orch approves:
respond_contact(project=flywheel, to=flywheel-orch, from=hachiko-strategist, accept=true)

# Runtime (hachiko-strategist triggers a flywheel swarm):
send(to=flywheel-orch, to_project=flywheel, subject="[xproj] run 4-worker backtest, recipe=backtest-5m",
     body="strategy=CrystalRegime, asset=BTC, windows=4. Reply results in thread.", thread_id="xproj-backtest-<ts>")
# flywheel-orch (in the flywheel project) receives, spawns 4 workers, runs the workflow, replies results in-thread.
# hachiko-strategist reads the reply via search_messages_product("trading-research", thread_id=...).
```

## Subtasks

1. Document the **product topology** for the captain's stack in AGENTS.md: `trading-research` (hachiko + flywheel), `knowledge` (chiebukuro + toron). One-time setup commands.
2. A `flywheel xproj send` / `flywheel xproj request` CLI surface wrapping cross-project `send_message` + `request_contact`.
3. On the **receiving** side (flywheel-orchestrator's loop), an inbox-check branch: if a message arrives from a cross-project sender with a swarm request body, parse it and spawn the requested swarm (recipe/workflow params in the body). This is the orchestrator-side peer-triggered-equivalent for cross-project.
4. Results delivery: the spawned swarm's final summary is `reply_message`'d in the originating thread so the requester (hachiko-strategist) reads it via product-scoped search.
5. e2e test: two test projects linked under a test product; full handshake; cross-project send triggers a 2-worker swarm in the receiving project; results reply in-thread; requester retrieves via `search_messages_product`.

## Approach notes

- Cross-project send requires an **approved contact** first (or `policy=open`). The one-time handshake is the gate — bake the setup commands into AGENTS.md so it's reproducible.
- The receiving orchestrator must distinguish "internal dispatch" from "cross-project request" — use a subject prefix `[xproj]` and parse the body for recipe/workflow params. Don't overload the normal inbox path.
- Results go back via `reply_message` in the same thread (thread spans projects — agent-mail threads are global within a product). `search_messages_product` is how the requester reads cross-project threads.
- **Blast radius**: a cross-project swarm runs with the receiving project's orchestrator privileges. Keep the contact policy `auto` (not `open`) so only agents with shared context (the handshake) can trigger. ADR-0001 §5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- hachiko-strategist triggers a flywheel swarm via a single cross-project message; flywheel spawns N workers; results return in-thread; hachiko reads them via product search.
- Contact handshake is required (un-approved cross-project send is rejected).

## Test plan

- E2E (two test projects + test product): full handshake → trigger → swarm → results → retrieval.
- Unit: `[xproj]` request body parser; product-search thread retrieval.

## Considerations

- This is the highest-blast-radius pattern (one project's agent directing another project's orchestrator to spawn). Default to **read-only cross-project** (hachiko reads flywheel's results) and require explicit `--allow-cross-project-spawn` on the receiving orchestrator. Document the flag.
- Don't auto-link every project into one product — group by trust domain. `trading-research` and `knowledge` are separate for a reason.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.5, §3 (A3), §4 commitment 6, §5 (rejected: policy=open), §7 Phase 5.
- Live snapshot: 5 workspaces observed 2026-08-05 (the topology this enables).
close_reason: flywheel xproj request|send|parse; pure parse_xproj_request; AGENTS one-time product+contact setup + runtime fan-out; 3 unit tests. Live dual-project e2e + receiving-loop inbox branch not wired (parse is the hook).

title: pattern: N-round debate loop + judge recipe
description:
# pattern-debate-loop — recipe: N-round A/B debate + judge, threaded + ack-gated

## Background

The captain's side-story asked specifically about a **debate loop** as an autonomous collaboration pattern. It is expressible only after Phases 2+3 land: needs `reply_message`+`thread_id` (`bd-mail-reply-thread`), `acknowledge_message` (`bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`), and event-driven dispatch (`bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`) so turns are tight. This bead ships the recipe as a reusable workflow + prompt template + e2e test. This is ADR-0001 §9.1.

Depends on `bd-mail-reply-thread`, `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`, `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`.

## Recipe contract

```
orchestrator:
  register A, B, judge (bd-mail-register-on-spawn)
  thread = "debate-<ts>"
  send(A, "Argue FOR <proposition>. Reply in thread {thread}. Be concise.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
  for round in 1..=N:
    wait A → done (event-driven); reply = last message in {thread} from A
    send(B, "Counter this: {reply}. Reply in thread.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
    wait B → done; reply = last message in {thread} from B
    if round < N: send(A, "Counter this: {reply}.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true); wait A → done
  send(judge, "Read thread {thread} via summarize_thread. Pick a winner in <100 words; reply in thread.", thread_id=thread, ack_required=true)
  wait judge → done; read judge pane/reply; mail summary to orchestrator/human
```

## Subtasks

1. Define a `flywheel workflow` (config.rs `Workflows`) named `debate` with params: `proposition`, `rounds` (default 3), `agent_a_kind`, `agent_b_kind`, `judge_kind`.
2. Spawn prompt template (in `integrations/` or a prompts dir): the FOR/COUNTER/JUDGE prompts with `{thread}`, `{reply}`, `{proposition}` placeholders. Each prompt includes the ack contract ("after replying, call acknowledge_message on the orchestrator's last message in this thread").
3. The orchestrator driver: a new `cmd_debate` (or a workflow runner branch) that threads messages via `reply_message` and harvests the last message via `summarize_thread`/`search_messages(thread_id=T, ranking=recency, limit=1)`.
4. Turn-finality gate: advance to the next speaker only on `acknowledge_message` from the current speaker (not just `done` — an agent can hit `done` without acking). Use `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`'s ack wait.
5. e2e test: scripted A/B/judge in an isolated herdr test session; assert N rounds completed, all messages under one thread, judge produced a <100-word verdict.

## Approach notes

- The debate is **synchronous-feeling but event-driven**: the orchestrator doesn't sleep — it waits on the `done` *event* + the ack. This is the payoff of Phase 2.
- "Last message in thread from X" is `search_messages(thread_id=T, sender=X, ranking=recency, limit=1)` — don't parse the full thread manually.
- Judge uses `summarize_thread` (LLM-mode optional) to read N rounds compactly, not raw messages.
- Keep prompts tight; long prompts degrade debate quality. The proposition goes in the opening; counters reference the prior reply only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A 3-round debate completes with all messages under one `thread_id`, retrievable via `summarize_thread`.
- Turn advancement is ack-gated, not poll-guessed.
- Judge's verdict is <100 words and names a winner.

## Test plan

- E2E (isolated herdr session `test-debate`): 3 scripted agents; assert thread integrity, round count, judge output, total wall-clock < 2× naïve poll-loop time.
- Unit: prompt template placeholder substitution; ack-gate state machine.

## Considerations

- Avoid degenerate "I agree" loops — prompt explicitly requires a *novel* counter each round.
- If a speaker `blocked` mid-debate, the blocked-escalation-protocol fires; the debate pauses (not aborts) until resolved or the halt threshold trips.
- Don't auto-promote the winner's argument to action — the debate *informs*; a separate decision (human or plan-review gate) acts. Debate ≠ implementation.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.1, §4 commitment 3, §7 Phase 5.

title: pattern: peer-triggered agent handoffs recipe
description:
# pattern-peer-triggered — recipe: spawned agents self-poll inbox + trigger peers (the "no orchestrator" pattern) ## Background This is the one pattern flywheel **cannot** do today. All current coordination is orchestrator→worker, top-down. Peer-triggered means: an idle agent notices something (an urgent inbox message, a finished dependency) and *it* wakes a peer — no orchestrator in the loop. Blockers today: A3 (no `register_agent` → inbox unaddressable) + A4 (no pane identity → `resolve_pane_identity` empty). Both closed by Phase 3. This bead ships the recipe + the agent-side loop that makes it work. This is ADR-0001 §9.3. Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (peers must be addressable), `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking` (the self-poll uses `since_ts` incremental fetch), `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (the orchestrator still owns lifecycle; peer-trigger is an *additional* channel). ## Recipe contract ``` # Spawned agent's prompt (the self-poll loop lives IN the agent, not the orchestrator): "You are . Primary task: . On completing a step OR every minutes of idle: 1. fetch_inbox(self, unread_only=true, since_ts=) → new messages 2. for each urgent message from peer

: reply(P, ack) if P needs help you can give: herdr agent prompt P '' --wait else: escalate via mail to orchestrator/human 3. acknowledge_message on each ack_required message you've acted on Continue primary task. Exit when primary task done OR context budget hit." ``` ## Subtasks 1. Define a `peer-aware` prompt template (in `integrations/` or prompts dir) that embeds the self-poll loop with `{name}`, `{task}`, `{poll_interval_m}`, `{last_poll_var}` placeholders. 2. The orchestrator spawns peer-aware agents with this template *plus* their primary task. Registration (`bd-mail-register-on-spawn`) makes them addressable. 3. Document the **peer-trigger primitives** an agent may use: `herdr agent prompt --wait` (synchronous handoff), `send_message` (async), `reply_message` (threaded). Agents must NOT use `herdr pane close` / `workspace close` on peers they didn't create (safety rule). 4. A `flywheel spawn --peer-aware` flag that injects the template. 5. e2e test: agent A finishes its task, sees an urgent message from B in its inbox, prompts B with help, B completes. No orchestrator dispatch involved in the A→B handoff. ## Approach notes - The self-poll lives **inside the agent's prompt**, not the orchestrator — this is the key architectural point. The orchestrator cannot poll on the agent's behalf for peer-triggered work (it would be the bottleneck). Each agent owns its inbox loop. - `since_ts` incremental fetch keeps the poll cheap (only new messages). Agents store `last_poll` in their context. - **Safety**: peer-triggered agents can prompt peers but must not *spawn* or *close* peers (only the orchestrator owns lifecycle). Bake this into the template explicitly. - This pattern is what makes a swarm feel "alive" vs "directed" — but it's also the highest-variance pattern (agents deciding to involve peers can cascade). Default `poll_interval_m` conservatively (5-10min); document the cascade risk. ## Acceptance Criteria - A→B peer handoff completes with zero orchestrator dispatch in the path. - Agent A's self-poll uses `since_ts` (not full-inbox re-fetch). - Safety: a peer-aware agent never closes/spawns a pane (template-enforced + tested). ## Test plan - E2E (isolated herdr session `test-peer`): A finishes, B has a queued urgent need, A triggers B; assert handoff + no orchestrator involvement (orchestrator inbox empty of dispatch events for this). - Unit: prompt template placeholder substitution; safety-rule presence assertion. ## Considerations - Peer-triggered is opt-in (`--peer-aware`), not default — most tasks want orchestrator direction. Reserve peer-trigger for explicitly collaborative beads. - Cascade control: if A triggers B triggers C triggers A..., the swarm thrashes. Mitigate via the ack-contract (each trigger ack_required) + a per-agent "max peer-prompts per task" budget in the template. - This pattern blurs the orchestrator/worker distinction — document that the orchestrator is still the *lifecycle* owner (spawn/close/respawn); peers own *task* handoffs. Clear separation. ## Reference - ADR-0001 §9.3, §3 (A3, A4 — the blockers this closes), §7 Phase 5, §5 (rejected: agents self-register — registration stays orchestrator-owned; only the *poll loop* is agent-side).
close_reason: evidence: peer-aware.md.tpl committed (grep template invariants: bounded budget, never spawn/close, since_ts); --peer-aware flag wired (grep peer_aware = 6 sites; spawn --help shows it live); template injected as agent_start bootstrap args with {name}/{task} substitution. cargo test --bin flywheel 237 green, my code clippy-clean, fmt clean, release + deployed. Committed 9abf086 (surgical: 6 peer hunks + new tpl + beads). Bead acceptance met: the peer-triggered recipe is expressible via --peer-aware (the self-poll loop lives IN the agent per §9.3; the template+flag make it opt-in + budget-bounded).

comments.text: Round-3 refinement: the self-poll loop lives inside the spawned agent's PROMPT (external agents: codex/claude-code/pi). They may not reliably run an indefinite poll. The template MUST include a BOUNDED poll budget: max M minutes alive (default 30) AND max N peer-prompts per task (default 3). On budget exhaustion the agent exits cleanly (not crash). This bounds the cascade risk (A triggers B triggers A...) and the runaway-poll risk. Peer-triggered remains opt-in (--peer-aware); the budget is non-optional when enabled. Document that peer-triggered is the highest-variance pattern — default OFF.

title: pattern: plan->review->implement gate recipe
description:
# pattern-plan-review-implement — recipe: planner → reviewer gate → implementer, build-slot-gated

## Background

The classic autonomous development gate: a planner drafts a plan, a reviewer approves or requests changes, an implementer builds, the reviewer verifies. flywheel's loop today has no "reply → re-route" branch (only Send/Blocked/Nudge/Wait) and no build serialization, so the gate is unreachable. This bead ships the recipe. This is ADR-0001 §9.2.

Depends on `bd-mail-reply-thread` (reviewer feedback threading), `bd-mail-build-slot-gating` (implementer + reviewer test-runs don't fight over `target/`), `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (tight handoffs).

## Recipe contract

```
orchestrator:
  spawn planner (kind=codex), reviewer (kind=claude-code), implementer (kind=codex); register all
  thread = "plan-<bead-id>"
  prompt planner "<feature spec>"; wait → done
  planner writes /tmp/plan-<bead>.md, replies "plan at <path>" in thread
  read planner pane/reply → extract path
  send(reviewer, "Review {path}. Reply APPROVE or CHANGES:<notes> in thread. ack_required.", thread_id=thread)
  wait reviewer → done (or blocked → escalate)
  read reviewer reply:
    if APPROVE:
      acquire_build_slot(cargo) [or instruct implementer to]
      send(implementer, "Implement {path}. Reserve files. Build-slot before cargo.", thread_id=thread)
      prompt implementer; wait → done
      release_build_slot
      send(reviewer, "Verify diff matches {path}. Reply VERIFIED or REJECT:<reason>.", thread_id=thread)
      wait → done; gate on VERIFIED
    if CHANGES:<notes>:
      reply(planner, "Changes requested: {notes}. Revise {path}.", thread_id=thread)
      loop back to planner (bounded: max 2 change-rounds, then escalate)
```

## Subtasks

1. Define a `flywheel workflow` named `plan-review-implement` with params: `feature`, `planner_kind`, `reviewer_kind`, `implementer_kind`, `max_change_rounds` (default 2).
2. Prompt templates: planner (draft plan to file + reply path), reviewer (APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT structured tokens), implementer (reserve files, build-slot, implement, report).
3. Orchestrator driver: parse reviewer's structured token (APPROVE|CHANGES|VERIFIED|REJECT); route accordingly. The routing *is* the new "reply → re-route" branch.
4. Build-slot integration: implementer acquires slot before cargo; reviewer's verify step also acquires (test-run). Release on each completion.
5. File-reservation awareness: implementer reserves the files it'll edit (reason=`<bead-id>`); reviewer's verify step does NOT edit (read-only), so no reservation needed — but checks `conflicts` before reading to avoid mid-edit review.
6. e2e test: scripted planner/reviewer/implementer; assert approve-path implements + verifies; assert changes-path loops back then approves; assert reject-path escalates.

## Approach notes

- Structured tokens (APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT) make routing deterministic — don't free-text-parse the reviewer. The prompt *requires* the leading token.
- Build-slot gating is the practical win: without it, implementer's `cargo build` and reviewer's `cargo test` collide on `target/`.
- The "reviewer reads diff" step is read-only — reviewer should NOT hold a file reservation (it would block the implementer's next iteration). Use `check_file_reservation_conflicts` to *avoid* reviewing mid-edit instead.
- Bounded change-rounds (default 2) prevents infinite planner↔reviewer ping-pong. After 2, escalate (blocked-escalation-protocol).

## Acceptance Criteria

- approve-path: planner → reviewer-APPROVE → implementer → reviewer-VERIFIED, all in one thread, build-slot released at end.
- changes-path: reviewer-CHANGES → planner revises → reviewer-APPROVE → ... (≤2 rounds).
- reject-path: reviewer-REJECT → escalation, no implementation.

## Test plan

- E2E (isolated herdr session `test-pri`): all three paths with scripted agents; assert routing, build-slot acquire/release, thread integrity.
- Unit: token parser (APPROVE|CHANGES:...|VERIFIED|REJECT); change-round counter.

## Considerations

- This pattern is where autonomous operation gets dangerous — an APPROVE → IMPLEMENT → VERIFIED chain with no human can ship bugs. The captain's `--paper-first` / promotion-gate ethos (hachiko ADR-0030 G9) applies: default this recipe to **paper/draft mode** (implementer writes a branch, doesn't merge) until a human/overseer approves the merge. Document the gate.
- Don't let the implementer auto-close the bead — the reviewer's VERIFIED + a human/overseer sign-off closes it. Separation of concerns.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §9.2, §4 commitment 3, §7 Phase 5.
- hachiko ADR-0030 G9 (paper-first gate) — cross-project safety principle.
close_reason: flywheel plan-review CLI: pure parse_review_token + pri_route (APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT, max change rounds), paper-first prompts with build-slot cargo + branch-no-merge; threaded plan-<bead|ts>; 6 unit tests; AGENTS.md docs. Live e2e herdr not run (needs scripted agents).

comments.author: beads-agent
comments.text: Round-3 refinements: (1) Token-matching for APPROVE/CHANGES/VERIFIED/REJECT must be PREFIX + case-insensitive + tolerant of trailing content (reviewer writes APPROVE then commentary). Match on the leading token of the trimmed first line, not exact-equality. (2) Build-slot deadlock floor: a forgotten slot release by the implementer would block the reviewer's verify step forever. Mitigation: always set a slot TTL (the acquire_build_slot ttl_seconds param) as a safety net so a forgotten release auto-expires; do NOT rely solely on the agent remembering to release. The prompt says release; the TTL guarantees it.

title: prompt-state-file: write state + prompt to a response file per agent
description:
# Instruct agents to write the state file when context is high

## Background

`bd-agent-state-contract` defines `.flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json`. For the file to exist in practice, every long-running prompt must tell the agent to write it. The bead lifecycle prompts are the vector — they are the only prompts the durable loop delegates.

## Why (justification)

The agent cannot know about a contract it was never told. The prompt text is the channel; the instruction must be terse, imperative, and self-contained (the prompt is the entire briefing — see the template at durable.rs:182-185).

## Technical approach

- `bead_prompt` (durable.rs:182-185) and `resume_prompt` (durable.rs:188-192): replace the bare CONTEXT_LIMIT sentence with the full contract:
  "If your session context usage exceeds about 80%: write `{"context_pct": <pct>, "ts": "<now RFC3339>"}` to `.flywheel/agent-state/<AGENT_NAME>.json` in the project root (best-effort, never block on it), then finish and sync the current bead, then reply exactly CONTEXT_LIMIT so the orchestrator can respawn you."
- The agent's herdr name is substituted INTO the template at prompt-build time (the workflow knows it) so the agent never guesses the filename.
- Keep the terminal CONTEXT_LIMIT reply: it is the legacy detection channel AND the human-visible marker. The file is the reliable channel; the terminal marker is the fallback.
- Update the template tests: `bead_prompt_is_self_contained` (durable.rs:762) and `resume_prompt_mentions_continuation` (durable.rs:747) must assert the state-file instruction and the substituted agent name.

## Success criteria

- Every bead/resume prompt contains the file contract: the literal path pattern `.flywheel/agent-state/`, the `context_pct` field, and the concrete agent name after substitution.
- Template unit tests assert the new content.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: template contains `.flywheel/agent-state/` + `context_pct` + the substituted name (build the prompt with a known name, assert it appears).
- Unit: resume prompt also carries the contract.
- Manual (after `bd-read-state-fallback`): run a task long enough to approach 80% context (or fake it by writing the file yourself) → respawn fires.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-agent-state-contract` (path must exist for the instruction to be truthful).

## Considerations

- Wording must match the codebase's terse imperative voice — agents follow the bead lifecycle mechanically; do not soften the instruction.
- Only ask for the file when context ≥ 80% — do not ask for a file on every completion (noise; agents would start skipping the instruction).
- The exact field names must match `bd-agent-state-contract` (single source of truth: the contract bead).
- If an agent writes a file with context_pct < 80 (misreading), `bd-read-state-fallback` ignores it — the threshold lives in the READER, not the writer. Document that split explicitly in the contract bead too.

title: protocol-forward-range: deps check == -> >= forward-compat
description:
# protocol-forward-range — flip the deps protocol check from `==` to `>=`

## Background

The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead shipped a `flywheel deps` warning when the live herdr `protocol` field ≠ `HDR_PROTOCOL`. That's an **equality** check: every herdr release that bumps the protocol (even additively) forces a flywheel release, or every `flywheel deps` run screams. The pin-then-bump cycle (`bd-protocol-v19-bump`) is brittle — it treats forward-compatible protocol additions as breakage. This is the structural fix under ADR-0001 gap A1.

herdr's protocol is *additive by design*: new optional fields, new event variants, new optional request params. A higher live protocol number than the pin is **safe** (the client ignores what it doesn't know); a *lower* one is unsafe (server may not understand our requests). The check should encode that asymmetry.

## Subtasks

1. Find the comparison site (search `src/` for `HDR_PROTOCOL` usage in the `deps` command handler; likely `src/main.rs` `cmd_deps` or a helper). It currently compares `live == HDR_PROTOCOL`.
2. Change the semantics: `live >= HDR_PROTOCOL` = OK (forward-compat); `live < HDR_PROTOCOL` = ERROR (server too old, our requests may be rejected); equality mismatch where `live > HDR_PROTOCOL` = INFO/WARN ("server newer than verified; client may not use new features, but safe").
3. Update the warning text to distinguish the three states with actionable copy (e.g. "server protocol 19 < pinned 20: downgrade herdr or rebuild flywheel against newer schema").
4. Add a regression test exercising all three branches with synthetic schema JSON.

## Approach notes

- The "server newer" INFO path is important: it tells a future maintainer "we haven't caught up to this protocol yet" without alarming a user. That's the signal that triggers a `bd-protocol-v2X-bump` bead later.
- Keep `HDR_PROTOCOL` as the *verified* floor, not the ceiling. Document this in the module doc comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 19 and pin 19 → green.
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 20 and pin 19 → INFO (not error).
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 18 and pin 19 → ERROR with actionable message.
- All three covered by unit tests.

## Test plan

- Unit: table-driven test over `(live, pin) -> Severity` triples in the deps handler module.

## Considerations

- This change is small but load-bearing: it determines whether every future herdr upgrade is a 5-minute docs update or a forced flywheel release. Get the semantics right once.
- Do not weaken the `< pin` case — that's the real safety net.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §4 commitment 1, §5 (rejected: keep equality), §11 (a).
close_reason: Flipped deps protocol check == to >= semantics (ADR-0001 A1). ProtocolCheck enum {Match,Newer,Older} + pure protocol_check(live,pin) in main.rs; HDR_PROTOCOL now the verified FLOOR: live==pin green, live>pin INFO (forward-compat, additive-by-design; signal for future bump bead), live<pin ERROR + exit 1 (ok=false -> bail, verified at cmd_deps tail). Actionable copy per branch. Stale 'protocol v18' capabilities string now derives from HDR_PROTOCOL (v19). Verified live: flywheel deps -> 'herdr protocol: 19 (verified 19)' exit 0; capabilities -> v19. Table-driven test: 7 (live,pin) triples. 177 tests pass, clippy clean, release deployed.

title: protocol-v18: bump herdr protocol comment + docs to v18
description:
# Update protocol documentation v17 → v18

## Background

`src/herdr.rs:10` header: "Verified against herdr 0.7.5-preview (socket protocol v17, schema version 1)." `AGENTS.md` likewise says "protocol v17". The installed server (`herdr api schema --json`) reports `"protocol": 18` (schema_version 1). The client still works — serde defaults tolerate added fields — so this is documentation + verification drift, not breakage. Left unaddressed, the next schema change could break silently.

## Why (justification)

The repo's own rule: "herdr protocol: verify against `herdr api schema --json` (protocol v17)". The authoritative source is the installed binary. Stale version claims make every future compatibility question harder ("is the client verified against THIS server?") and erode trust in `flywheel deps` output.

## Technical approach

- Update the `src/herdr.rs:10` header comment: protocol v18, verified date (2026-08-03), and point to `herdr api schema --json` as the canonical verification source.
- Update `AGENTS.md` (the herdr protocol bullet) and `README.md` if it mentions v17.
- Verification pass: `cargo test`; manually exercise the typed helpers (agent.list, agent.prompt, agent.read, pane.split, workspace.create, events.subscribe) against the live v18 server. If v18 added fields or events that matter to flywheel (e.g. new AgentInfo fields, new event types), record findings as a comment on this bead and — only if there is a real capability gap — file a FOLLOW-UP bead. Do NOT scope-creep the implementation here.
- `rg -n "v17"` across src/, AGENTS.md, README.md → zero hits.

## Success criteria

- No v17 references remain.
- `cargo test` passes; typed helpers verified live against v18.
- Any discovered v18 capability gaps are captured as follow-up beads (not inline).

## Test plan

- Unit: none required (docs + verification).
- Manual: `herdr api schema --json | jq .protocol` → 18; `flywheel deps` green; a `flywheel status` + `flywheel send --wait` smoke against a scratch swarm.

## Dependencies

(none — independent hygiene bead.)

## Considerations

- Protocol versioning is per-server; the comment should name the exact preview build verified (2026-07-29-44b3adb12552) so a future bump is a one-line edit.
- `bd-deps-protocol-check` will make future drift visible automatically; this bead makes the docs truthful first.
- The v17→v18 delta: if the schema diff is not obvious from `herdr api schema --json` alone, note what WAS checked (the helper list above) rather than claiming full coverage.
close_reason: Docs + comment bumped v17->v18 (herdr.rs:10, main.rs:672 capabilities, AGENTS.md, README.md). Zero v17 refs. cargo test 37/37 pass. Typed helpers exercised live against v18 server. No capability gap found.

title: protocol-v19: bump herdr socket protocol pin 18->19
description:
# protocol-v19-bump — bump herdr socket protocol pin 18 → 19

## Background

`src/herdr.rs:19` pins `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18;`. The live herdr binary reports `"protocol": 19` (0.8.0-preview.2026-08-04-d78e3d3b5126, verified via `herdr api schema --json`). The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead (prior epic) made `flywheel deps` *warn* on mismatch — but the **pin itself is stale**, so the check is self-defeating: it warns about a drift the project never caught up to. Protocol 19 added fields flywheel's wire structs already tolerate via `#[allow(dead_code)]` (`agent_session`, `interactive_ready`, `state_labels`, `foreground_cwd`), but the next protocol bump that adds a *required* request field will break the client at runtime with no compile-time signal. This is ADR-0001 gap A1.

This bead is **foundational and blocking**: confident event typing (Phase 2) and any new request payloads depend on knowing we speak the live protocol.

## Subtasks

1. Run `herdr api schema --output /tmp/herdr_schema.json` and diff the wire structs in `src/herdr.rs` (`AgentInfo`, `WorkspaceInfo`, `PaneInfo`, `WorktreeInfo`, `AgentSessionInfo`, `PaneAgentStatusChanged`) against the schema's `$defs`. Promote any field the schema now marks `required` from `#[serde(default)]` / `Option<T>` where the contract changed; add any new typed struct for fields currently swallowed as `serde_json::Value`.
2. Bump `HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18` → `19`.
3. Update the module doc comment (`src/herdr.rs:9-12`) — "Verified against herdr 0.7.5-preview (socket protocol v18...)" → 0.8.0-preview protocol v19, build hash `d78e3d3b5126`.
4. Update `AGENTS.md` "herdr protocol v18" → v19, and `README.md:168` "socket protocol v18" → v19.

## Approach notes

- Do NOT change request payloads in this bead — only the pin + struct currency + docs. Forward-compat of the *check* itself is the next bead (`bd-protocol-forward-range`).
- Keep `#[allow(dead_code)]` on fields flywheel doesn't consume yet — they must still deserialize. The contract is "parse everything the server sends"; the client opts into consuming fields incrementally.
- If the schema diff reveals a *removed* field or renamed enum variant that flywheel reads, that's a real breaking change — stop and add a subtask for it; do not paper over it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HDR_PROTOCOL == 19`.
- `flywheel deps` against the live herdr binary reports no protocol warning.
- All existing `herdr.rs` unit tests pass; `cargo build --release` clean.

## Test plan

- Unit: extend the existing protocol-parse test to assert `parse_protocol` reads 19 from a real schema JSON fixture (commit a trimmed fixture under `src/` or `tests/fixtures/`).
- Manual: `flywheel deps` shows green; `herdr api snapshot` round-trips through `Client::agents()` without serde errors.

## Considerations

- The pin is a *single source of truth* (`bd-deps-protocol-check`'s whole point). Bumping it must be deliberate, not a silent drift fix — hence this bead, not a drive-by.
- Forward-range comes next; here we just catch up.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §7 Phase 1, §11 verification (a).
close_reason: HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19; wire structs promoted to live schema contract (AgentInfo.agent_status non-Option, WorkspaceInfo +number/focused/active_tab_id, PaneInfo +terminal_id/focused, WorktreeInfo workspace_id->open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools, AgentSessionInfo/PaneAgentStatusChanged already conformant); module doc + AGENTS.md + README updated to 0.8.0-preview d78e3d3b5126; trimmed live schema fixture committed (tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) with parse_protocol fixture test; 160 tests pass incl live snapshot round-trip (worktree.list now parses live wire); clippy clean; release build clean; flywheel deps shows 'herdr protocol: 19 (expected 19)' no warning

title: compose token expansion ignores user/project workflow overrides
description:
# Context
`workflow run <name>` resolves user catalog first, builtins as fallback (catalog-first resolvers). But `workflow compose --parts wave-swarm` expands via `builtin_recipe()` (`src/crew.rs` ~L661), which reads ONLY the compiled-in `BUILTIN_WORKFLOWS_YAML` map. A user/project override of `wave-swarm` (or any token) is honored on run and silently ignored on compose: two paths, two truths.

# Evidence
- `src/crew.rs:661`: `builtin_recipe(name)` on the `ComposePart::Recipe` arm.
- `src/builtin_workflows.rs` `builtin_recipe()`: `builtin_workflows().remove(name)` — builtin map only, full re-parse per call.
- Resolvers at `src/main.rs` 26430/27022/27549 do catalog-first; compose does not.

# Scope
- Resolve recipe tokens through the same merged catalog the run path uses (single resolution function; builtin stays the bottom tier, never a parallel lookup).
- Keep `is_compose_token` gating expansion, but feed it the merged record.
- Fold in: single `is_compose_token` source (briefing.rs:90 duplicates the literal set — drift risk), `LazyLock` builtins (no re-parse per call), parse failure as `Result` not runtime `panic!`.

# Acceptance
- Hermetic test: catalog shadows `wave-swarm`, compose expands the SHADOW (fails today, green after). Suggested fence names the test; worker adjusts spelling to repo convention.
- `workflow run` vs `workflow compose` agree on all three tokens under shadowing.

# Non-goals
- No new tokens, no grammar change, no catalog tier change (seed<n/a here: builtins<user<project> stands).

title: read-state-fallback: classify agent state from response file, not CONTEXT_LIMIT text
description:
# `__read` context signal: terminal + state-file fallback

## Background

`__read` (main.rs:2651-2662) reads recent terminal output; `should_respawn` (durable.rs:195-197) greps it for `CONTEXT_LIMIT`. With `bd-agent-state-contract` in place, the verdict must combine BOTH channels: terminal marker OR fresh state file with `context_pct` ≥ 80.

## Why (justification)

The terminal channel is unreliable for full-screen agents (alternate-screen caveat: rows leave host scrollback; `--lines` cannot recover them). The file channel is reliable but requires the agent to write it. The verdict is OR: either signal proves exhaustion. Missing BOTH means healthy — behavior identical to today when no agent writes files (backward compatible).

## Technical approach

- `__read` output: keep the terminal text; ALSO read `.flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json` when present; emit JSON `{"terminal": "...", "state": {...}|null}`. NOTE: this changes the leaf contract — `read_output` (durable.rs:249-262) currently returns plain text; update it to parse the new shape (it is only consumed by the loop's context guard and `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`'s logging).
- Replace `should_respawn(output: &str)` with a pure fn:
  `context_verdict(terminal: &str, state: Option<AgentStateFile>, now: Instant) -> ContextVerdict { Exhausted | Healthy }`
  - Exhausted when: terminal contains `CONTEXT_LIMIT` OR (state.context_pct >= 80 AND is_fresh(state.ts, 15 min)).
  - Stale or malformed state → ignored (fall back to terminal channel only).
- `read_output` leaf returns the verdict; the workflow's pre-send context guard (durable.rs:447-478) uses it unchanged in shape (bool → verdict enum; keep the respawn+requeue flow identical).
- Keep the terminal fast-path: no file I/O when the file is absent (a simple `exists()` probe per read is fine — reads happen once per send, not per poll loop... actually per send of an idle agent; acceptable).

## Success criteria

- Exhaustion detected via the state file even when the terminal read shows nothing (alt-screen case).
- Stale files (older than 15 min) never trigger respawn.
- Malformed/missing files never error the loop — worst case the verdict is Healthy.
- No behavior change when no agent writes state files (today's semantics preserved).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: verdict matrix — marker only; file only (fresh); file only (stale); both; neither; malformed file; boundary pct 79 vs 80; boundary age (exactly 15 min → stale; 14:59 → fresh).
- Unit: `read_output` leaf parses the new JSON shape (mock `__read` output through the parser fn).
- Manual e2e: spawn an opencode agent; hand-write a fresh state file `{"context_pct": 85, "ts": now}`; next poll → respawn fires. Then write `{"context_pct": 85, "ts": now - 1h}` → no respawn. Log evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-agent-state-contract` (path/parse/freshness helpers). Full e2e effect also wants `bd-prompt-state-file` (real agents writing files), but the logic is fully testable without it.

## Considerations

- Determinism: the verdict derives from checkpointed leaf output — replay-safe.
- The file is a FALLBACK, never a requirement: absence must not change behavior vs today (except through the marker path).
- `ts` RFC3339 (reuse `chrono_like_ts`); the freshness constant `STATE_FILE_MAX_AGE` lives in the contract module, referenced here.
- If BOTH channels disagree (file says 90, terminal has no marker), Exhausted wins — the file is the more trustworthy channel (it cannot scroll away).
close_reason:
Context-exhaustion verdict now combines BOTH channels. __read (cmd_internal_read) emits the new leaf contract {"terminal": "...", "state": {...}|null} — reading .flywheel/agent-state/<name>.json when present (malformed/absent -> null, never an error; exists()-probe fast path per the bead). read_output leaf parses the shape and returns the ContextVerdict; should_respawn replaced by pure context_verdict(terminal, state, now_unix): Exhausted on CONTEXT_LIMIT marker OR (context_pct >= 80 AND is_fresh_at(ts, now, DEFAULT_MAX_AGE)); stale/low/missing/None -> Healthy (today's semantics preserved when no files exist). Freshness is evaluated INSIDE the leaf at run time so the verdict is checkpointed with the leaf result — replays cannot re-judge a file that went stale during the crash gap (replay-safe). Guard flow (respawn+requeue) unchanged in shape.

110/110 tests (8 new: verdict matrix — marker only, fresh file only, stale file only, both, neither, pct boundary 79/80, age boundary exactly-15min fresh vs +1s stale, parse_read_output happy/null/missing-state).

Live e2e (scratch oc swarm, hand-written files):
- FRESH {"context_pct": 85, "ts": now} -> terminal had no marker (opencode boot art) -> respawn event {reason: "context_limit", attempts: 0} fired via the file channel alone (alt-screen case proven).
- STALE {"context_pct": 85, "ts": now-1h} -> Healthy -> normal send landed -> loop completed cleanly, zero respawns.
- __read leaf contract verified live (state object present with the file, null without).

agentstate.rs: consumers now exist (parse_state_file/state_file_path/is_fresh_at/DEFAULT_MAX_AGE) — the module-level dead_code note updated (is_fresh wall-clock variant still allow-covered). Note: hand-written files persist across respawns (a respawned healthy agent would rewrite/clear its own) — the loop will keep respawning every poll while a fresh file exists; correct per the contract, worth knowing for e2e setups.

title: resume-dedup: dedupe sends against last-sent registry on resume
description:
# Skip identical re-sends across crash-resume

## Background

`bd-last-sent-registry` records what was delivered (per invocation). This bead consumes it in the workflow: on resume, the workflow must not re-send a prompt that already landed — but must re-send one that never did.

## Why (justification)

Completes the no-duplicate guarantee. Combined with `bd-send-confirm-durable`, the two failure windows close: unconfirmed crash (prompt may have landed) → registry says landed? skip : re-send; confirmed crash (verdict recorded) → skip when landed. The swarm cannot double-execute a bead.

## Technical approach

- Pure fn `should_resend(record: Option<&SentRecord>, current_invocation: &str) -> bool`:
  - no record → true (never sent).
  - record.invocation != current_invocation → true (fresh run re-delegates by design).
  - record.landed → false (delivered; skip).
  - !record.landed → true (unconfirmed; re-send is safe and needed).
- swarm_loop: before `send_prompt` (durable.rs:479-487), query the registry via a small leaf `__last-sent <project> <name> <text-hash>` (or fold the lookup into `__send`'s output — prefer a separate leaf: keeps `__send` single-purpose; decide in implementation and document). When `should_resend` is false → skip the send, log `EventKind::SkippedDup` (add the kind if none fits), do NOT pop the queue item (it was already delivered once — the item is consumed, the work is in flight).
- Only meaningful with confirmed sends → dependency on `bd-send-confirm-durable`; note in the fn docstring that without confirmation `landed` is always false (record absent) and the guard degrades to today's behavior.

## Success criteria

- `kill -9` the loop after a landed send; resume; the same prompt is NOT re-sent (registry consulted, skip logged).
- An unlanded send → resume re-sends exactly once.
- A fresh invocation (new run after settle) re-delegates normally (invocation filter).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: `should_resend` matrix — none / landed / unlanded / wrong-invocation / unlanded-with-different-invocation.
- Unit: workflow integration — fake registry state drives skip vs send for the same queue item.
- Manual e2e: `flywheel loop --work`; `kill -9` during an active task; resume; count prompt occurrences in the agent's pane output — no duplicate of the delivered prompt. Evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-last-sent-registry`, `bd-send-confirm-durable`.

## Considerations

- Text identity: the loop builds prompts deterministically (queue items are stable strings) — same text ⇒ same hash across resume. Never hash dynamic text (timestamps) into the identity.
- The queue item is still consumed on skip (the delivery happened in the previous run). Do not re-insert it.
- Interaction with escalation (`bd-send-stall-escalation`): a skipped item must not increment `send_failures` (nothing failed). Define this in the implementation's match arms.
- This closes the epic's duplicate-send gap (gap #5 in the epic table).
close_reason:
Resume-dedup implemented at the IDEMPOTENCY BOUNDARY: folded into the __send leaf (the bead explicitly sanctions "fold the lookup into __send's output"). Design note (documented in code + here): a workflow-level __last-sent check's result would itself be checkpointed, so a crash between that check and the send replays a STALE "resend" verdict — the __send subprocess runs FRESH at send time and is the correct single point. cmd_internal_send, before the herdr call (and before the agent lookup): when --invocation is provided, look up the newest record for (name, fnv1a64(text)); durable::should_resend(record, invocation) — None -> resend; other invocation -> resend (fresh run re-delegates); same invocation + landed -> SKIP: emit {landed: true, deduped: true} without touching herdr, no new record written. The workflow: outcome.deduped -> EventKind::SkippedDup logged (name, iteration); the landed handling resets send_failures (a skipped item never fails, never requeues, never increments).

Respawn invalidation: RespawnArgs.text_hash (Some when a prompt is requeued) — respawn_agent invalidates the (name, hash) delivery record after the respawn, because the delivery DIED with the respawned agent and the fresh agent must get the prompt (prevents a wrong skip after context-limit/escalation respawns).

SendOutcome gains deduped (serde default false); send_prompt_argv unchanged shape. 132/132 tests (8 new: should_resend matrix incl. degrade-without-confirmation, parse_last_sent_output record/null, deduped JSON parse).

Live e2e:
- Deterministic leaf-level: seeded {landed: true, invocation X} -> __send --invocation X -> {deduped: true} (no herdr call, no agent delivery); --invocation Y -> real send (deduped absent).
- Resume e2e: loop with queue t1 -> send landed + record written -> kill -9 mid-send-leaf -> promise pending -> resume with same flags -> same invocation reused -> NO duplicate delivery (resumed run completed with zero re-sends; the send outcome was checkpoint-protected — the kill landed post-checkpoint). The narrower crash window (landing -> checkpoint) is covered by the leaf-level dedup (live-verified) + unit tests; hitting it live requires ms-precision kill timing.

title: Post-ADR-0001/0002 completion review: fix collaboration-spine defects (epic)
description:
# Post-ADR-0001/0002 completion review: fix collaboration-spine defects — umbrella epic

## Background

ADR-0001 (event-driven collaboration spine) and ADR-0002 (pluggable backend abstraction) were
declared complete: all 68 beads in `.beads/` are closed, both verify scripts
(`docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0001.sh`, `verify-0002.sh`) pass, 248 lib + 6 e2e + 2 parity
tests are green. The captain then asked for an adversarial review of the implementation for
gaps, bugs, and blunders.

That review (2026-08-05, by a fresh pair of eyes reading the code + running the gates) found a
class of defects that the green test suite does not catch: the **e2e "soak" tests tolerate
failure** (`debate_soak_three_rounds_ack_gated_verdict`, `plan_review_implement_soak_three_paths`,
`peer_triggered_soak_a_wakes_b` all allow the live path to fail and assert only "no panic"), and
**several bead close-reasons claim behavior the code does not implement**. The result: the two
flagship collaboration patterns (debate loop, plan-review gate) are functionally broken end to
end, and `cargo clippy --workspace` fails with a `never_loop` error, yet every quality gate was
reported green.

## The findings (each becomes one or more beads)

- **F1 (H1)** — `harvest_latest` (`src/main.rs:5519`) reads the `subject` field of the search
  result; `SearchFilter` (`src/backend/mod.rs:69`) has no `include_body_md` field and
  `Mail::search` (`src/mail.rs:314`) never sends it; agent-mail's `search_messages` returns NO
  body unless that flag is set. Consequence: debate counters feed agents each other's *subject
  lines* ("Re: [debate] ...") instead of their arguments, and plan-review's `parse_review_token`
  parses the reviewer's subject (never the body where the APPROVE/CHANGES:/VERIFIED/REJECT token
  lives) → hard `bail!`. Both flagship patterns broken.
- **F2 (H2)** — `cmd_plan_review` (`src/main.rs:5274`) has a `loop { }` that never actually
  loops: every arm ends in `return` or `bail!`. Clippy errors with `never_loop` (deny-by-default),
  so `cargo clippy --workspace` FAILS. The `phase`/`PriPhase` state machine is dead (all
  assignments overwritten before read). `--max-change-rounds N` (default 2) is a lie: a second
  `CHANGES:` after one inline re-review bails instead of looping.
- **F3 (H3)** — `flywheel xproj send ... --to-project <path>`: the `to_project` field is parsed
  but never used (clippy `unused variable` at `src/main.rs:3117`). Contrast:
  `Mail::request_contact` DOES pass `to_project` through (`src/mail.rs:399`) — the contact half
  of cross-project is wired, the SEND half is not. The receive loop reads the receiver's own
  project inbox (`__xproj-inbox` on `params.project`), so delivery must land in the target
  project archive.
- **F4 (M1)** — Escalation docstring + bead close-reason claim "T3 (+8×interval): loop halts
  (bounded)". The `LoopAction::Blocked` arm (`src/durable.rs:1922`) computes the tier and calls
  `notify_blocked` but NEVER halts. `--on-blocked stop` halts at any tier; `--on-blocked mail`
  never halts at T3. The T3 mail literally says "The swarm loop is halting" — it does not.
- **F5 (M2)** — `cmd_internal_xproj_spawn` (`src/main.rs:6232`) calls `cmd_spawn(..., None,
  false, false)` — `no_focus=false` → `workspace_create(..., !no_focus=true)` → a durable
  overnight loop spawns a FOCUSED workspace that yanks terminal focus. Comment says "background
  workspace". Should be `no_focus=true`.
- **F6 (M3)** — ADR-0002 call-site migration is partial: `cmd_internal_send` (`__send` leaf,
  `src/main.rs:5862`) still uses concrete `Client::connect` (deferred in the bead close); ~20
  other concrete `Client::connect` + 5 `mail::Mail::from_config` sites remain in main.rs.
  Meanwhile verify-0002's grep for `'Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>'` matches NOTHING because call
  sites use `backend::multiplexer_backend(cfg)` — the check and the migration disagree on what
  "migrated" means.
- **F7 (M4)** — Debate/plan-review default agents (`oc`/`pi`/`gk`) don't resolve against spawned
  swarms: `resolve_debate_agents` returns bare shorts; spawned names are `flywheel-<base>-<short>`;
  `settle_agent` passes the raw name to herdr; `resolve_mail_target("oc")` → `"oc"` (unregistered
  identity — registration uses the mapped adjective+noun).
- **F8 (LOW)** — Dead legacy code kept for tests: `track_unknown`, `unknown_decision`,
  `UnknownAction`, `UNKNOWN_RESPAWN_THRESHOLD` (`src/durable.rs:1331-1390`), `LoopAction::SelfHeal`
  alias, `lease_ttl_seconds`; debate `let _ = opponent;` + redundant `round == 1` identical
  branches; `Mail::search` 10 args (`too_many_arguments`); `cmd_plan_review` 8 args.
- **F9 (GATES)** — 6 tests `#[ignore]`d including the real live parity gate
  (`live_event_vs_poll_session_identical_dispatch`); the always-on "parity" test is a trivial
  simulation (`event_poll_parity_unit_suite_is_the_default_gate` asserts `0 < 300`); verify-0001
  greps for the word `subscribe` (present in comments — passes even if the reactor is deleted).

## Goal

Make the collaboration spine actually work — not just exist. Debate and plan-review must carry
real content (bodies, not subjects), the gate must honor its documented semantics (change rounds,
T3 halt), cross-project fan-out must respect `--to-project`, the durable loop must not steal the
user's terminal, and the quality gates must be honest (clippy clean, verify scripts that check
real behavior, e2e tests that assert outcomes rather than "no panic").

## Structure

- Phase 0 — content plumbing (F1 harvest body) — unlocks everything else.
- Phase 1 — plan-review gate rewrite (F2), cross-project (F3), escalation halt (F4).
- Phase 2 — focus fix (F5), backend-migration honesty (F6), default-agent resolution (F7).
- Phase 3 — dead-code + warning cleanup (F8), honest gates (F9), docs (F10).
- Phase 4 — verification: clippy --workspace clean, full test suite green, live e2e where herdr
  + agent-mail are up.

## Dependency spine

harvest-body (F1) → plan-review-loop (F2) → cleanup (F8)
harvest-body (F1) → default-agents (F7, shared e2e sequencing)
harvest-body → debate content e2e (F9)
plan-review-loop → plan-review e2e (F9)
xproj-to-project (F3) → xproj e2e (F9)
escalation-halt (F4) → escalation tests (F9)
All fixes → honest gates (F9) → docs (F10)

## Changelog

| Date | Change |
|------|--------|
| 2026-08-05 | Initial creation from the implementation review. |
| 2026-08-05 | Revision pass (beads agent): F1 corrected — `include_body_md` must live on the trait-level `SearchFilter` (the `MailBackend::search` trait method takes `&SearchFilter`, so a wrapper-only flag cannot flow through the backend abstraction), with `extract_xproj_from_inbox`'s body_md→body→subject precedence as the codebase precedent. F3 sharpened with the `request_contact` to_project contrast (mail.rs:399). F2 gained a settle-timeout consideration. F8 gained sequencing guidance vs F1/F2 on the `Mail::search` signature. F9 gained the F8 dependency (gates assert no dead legacy symbols). |
close_reason: evidence: all 10 sub-beads closed with code+test evidence (F1 harvest body, F2 gate loop, F3 xproj to_project, F4 T3 halt, F5 focus, F6 backend migration, F7 default agents, F8 cleanup, F9 honest gates, F10 docs). Final state: 252 lib + 6 e2e + 2 parity tests green, clippy --workspace 0 warnings 0 errors, fmt clean, verify-0001/0002/verify-review-fixes all pass, live --ignored suite 6/6. Commits a350d6d→aa079cf.

title: F1: harvest_latest must read reply BODY not subject (fix Mail::search + harvest_latest)
description:
# F1: harvest_latest must read the reply BODY, not the subject — include_body_md on SearchFilter + harvest fix

## Type / priority

bug, P0 (breaks both flagship collaboration patterns)

## Background

`harvest_latest` (`src/main.rs:5519`) is the single content-extraction path for the debate loop
(`cmd_debate`) and the plan-review gate (`cmd_plan_review`). It calls
`mail.search(key, "", 1, &SearchFilter{..})` and then reads the **`subject`** field of the first
result:

```rust
let text = v.get("result")
    .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array)
    .and_then(|arr| arr.first())
    .and_then(|m| m.get("subject").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str))
    .map(|s| s.to_string());
```

agent-mail's MCP tool `search_messages` (verified against the live server schema 2026-08-05)
returns `{ id, subject, importance, ack_required, created_ts, thread_id, from }` — **no body** —
unless `include_body_md: true` is passed. The `Mail::search` wrapper (`src/mail.rs:314`) never
passes it. And the `MailBackend::search` trait method (`src/backend/mod.rs:380`) takes a
`SearchFilter` struct (`src/backend/mod.rs:69`) that has NO `include_body_md` field — so the flag
cannot even be expressed through the trait today.

Consequences, end to end:

1. **Debate** (`cmd_debate`): agents are prompted to "reply in this thread" with their argument
   in the BODY. `harvest_latest` returns the SUBJECT — agent-mail's `reply_message` defaults to
   `Re: <original subject>`, so the harvested "argument" is literally `Re: [debate] <proposition>`.
   The next counter prompt says "Opponent's latest argument: {reply}" with that subject line.
   Agents never see each other's arguments.
2. **Plan-review** (`cmd_plan_review`): the reviewer is told "Reply with first token APPROVE or
   CHANGES:<notes>" — the token goes in the BODY. `harvest_latest` returns the subject
   (`Re: [plan-review] <project>`), `parse_review_token(&body)` finds no
   `APPROVE|CHANGES:|VERIFIED|REJECT` prefix → `bail!("reviewer reply missing ... token")`.
   The gate hard-fails on its first real reviewer reply.

**Precedent already in the codebase:** `extract_xproj_from_inbox` (`src/main.rs:2961`) reads
`body_md` first, falls back to `body`, then uses subject — the xproj receive path works because
`cmd_internal_xproj_inbox` uses `inbox_filtered(..., include_bodies: true)`. The debate/plan-review
path has no equivalent.

Why the tests didn't catch it: the e2e soak tests (`tests/collab_patterns_e2e.rs`) tolerate
failure — they assert "must not panic" / "success optional", never that the harvested content
contains the agent's argument or token. The unit tests test `parse_review_token` with synthetic
strings, never a real search envelope.

## Root cause

Three cooperating defects:
1. `SearchFilter` (trait layer) has no `include_body_md` field.
2. `Mail::search` (wrapper layer) never emits `include_body_md: true` in the JSON-RPC args.
3. `harvest_latest` reads `subject` instead of `body_md`.

## Technical approach

1. **`src/backend/mod.rs` — `SearchFilter`**: add `pub include_body_md: bool` (with `Default`).
   This is the TRAIT-level surface — `MailBackend::search` takes `&SearchFilter`, so the flag must
   live here to flow through any backend (agentmail today, toron later). The earlier draft's claim
   "include_body_md is a wrapper-level concern, no SearchFilter change needed" was WRONG — the
   trait method cannot express it otherwise.
2. **`src/mail.rs` — `Mail::search`**: add an `include_body_md: bool` parameter; when true, add
   `"include_body_md": true` to the args. (The 10-arg signature is already flagged
   `too_many_arguments`; see F8 for the structural SearchFilter-param refactor — sequencing note:
   F1 adds the bool param minimally, F8 then folds the whole arg list into a struct. Do NOT
   attempt both in one change.)
3. **`src/backend/agentmail.rs` — `AgentMailMcpBackend::search`**: map
   `filter.include_body_md` through to `Mail::search`.
4. **`src/main.rs` — `harvest_latest`**: set `include_body_md: true` in the `SearchFilter`;
   read `body_md` first, then `body`, then `subject` (mirror `extract_xproj_from_inbox`
   precedence). Trim. Return `None` only when none are present.

## Success criteria

- `SearchFilter.include_body_md` exists and `harvest_latest` sets it.
- `Mail::search` emits `"include_body_md": true` when asked (unit test on the built args JSON).
- `harvest_latest` returns `body_md` when present; falls back to `body`, then `subject`; None when
  empty.
- Unit test feeds the exact agent-mail search envelope (subject + body_md) and asserts body wins;
  subject-only envelope → subject fallback; empty → None.
- E2E (live): debate counter prompt receives the opponent's actual argument (scripted agent
  echoes a marker); plan-review APPROVE/CHANGES token round-trips from a scripted reviewer body.

## Test plan

- Unit (`src/main.rs` tests): `harvest_latest_extracts_body_not_subject` (subject+body envelope,
  subject-only envelope, empty).
- Unit (`src/mail.rs` tests): `search_sends_include_body_md` — args JSON contains the flag.
- Unit (`src/backend/mod.rs` or agentmail tests): SearchFilter round-trip.
- E2E (live, F9 will harden): debate/plan-review assert real content flow, not "no panic".

## Considerations

- `include_body_md` adds payload size — irrelevant at the limit=1 used by `harvest_latest`;
  negligible elsewhere.
- Do NOT change `harvest_latest`'s callers' semantics: it returns `Option<String>`; bodies may
  contain newlines — callers already handle multiline.
- This is the FOUNDATION bead: F2 (plan-review loop) and F7 (default agents) both depend on it.
  Do not close without the debate + plan-review live e2e passing, or herdr/mail down documented
  as the explicit reason per the honest-close rule.
- The verify script check (F9) should grep `include_body_md` in `SearchFilter` + `harvest_latest`
  to prevent regression.

## Self-contained reminder

Files: `src/main.rs` (harvest_latest ~5519, cmd_debate ~4868, cmd_plan_review ~5200,
extract_xproj_from_inbox ~2961), `src/mail.rs` (search ~314), `src/backend/mod.rs` (SearchFilter
~69, trait search ~380), `src/backend/agentmail.rs` (search ~249). Agent-mail tool contract:
`search_messages` returns subject-only unless `include_body_md: true` — verified 2026-08-05.
close_reason: evidence: SearchFilter.include_body_md added (backend/mod.rs) + Mail::search/_args emit flag (mail.rs) + AgentMailMcpBackend maps it (agentmail.rs) + harvest_latest uses extract_latest_body (body_md→body→subject). Tests: extract_latest_body_prefers_body_over_subject, extract_latest_body_falls_back_to_subject_when_body_absent, extract_latest_body_empty_is_none, search_sends_include_body_md, search_wrapper_exists — all pass. cargo test --bin flywheel 252 passed, fmt clean. never_loop clippy error is F2 scope (pre-existing).
