title: F2: cmd_plan_review gate loop never loops — rewrite as real state machine honoring max_change_rounds
description:
# F2: cmd_plan_review gate loop never loops — rewrite as a real state machine honoring max_change_rounds

## Type / priority

bug, P0 (clippy compile ERROR + broken ADR-0001 §9.2 contract)

## Background

`cmd_plan_review` (`src/main.rs:5274`) declares `loop { match &action { ... } }` but every arm
ends in `return Ok(())` or `bail!` — no path continues back to the loop head. Clippy
(deny-by-default `never_loop`) fails the build:

```
error: this loop never actually loops
  --> src/main.rs:5274:5
```

The `phase` variable (`PriPhase`) is assigned in every arm and never read — clippy flags
"value assigned to `phase` is never read" ×5. The `PriPhase`/`PriAction` state machine in
`pri_route` is bypassed by inline duplicated code. The telltale comment: "// recurse one review
by continuing loop with synthetic action // simplest: re-send and continue parsing at top via
goto-style" — the implementer meant to loop, inlined one review cycle, and never looped back.

Consequences:
- `--max-change-rounds N` (default 2) is NOT honored. The planner↔reviewer CHANGES cycle runs at
  most ONCE (inline). A second `CHANGES:` after the inline re-review hits
  `bail!("after second review only APPROVE/REJECT/CHANGES expected")` — a hard error, not a loop.
- ADR-0001 §9.2 contract violated: "CHANGES → reply planner with changes; loop back to planner".
- The clippy gate (`cargo clippy --workspace` clean, documented in AGENTS.md) is RED.
- `unreachable!()` matches exist where the code asserts "the only action after pri_after_plan is
  PromptReviewer" — a logic change elsewhere would panic instead of erroring.

The unit tests (`pri_route_changes_then_exhaust`, `pri_route_approve_path`,
`pri_route_reject_escalates`) test the pure `pri_route` function — which is CORRECT — but never
test the driver's loop behavior. That is why the defect shipped.

## Technical approach

Rewrite the driver body of `cmd_plan_review` as a genuine phase-driven loop:

```rust
let mut phase = PriPhase::AwaitingPlanReview;
let mut change_rounds = 0;
loop {
    let action = match phase {
        PriPhase::AwaitingPlanReview => /* send reviewer prompt, settle, harvest, parse token,
                                           pri_route(...) → set phase+change_rounds, continue */
        PriPhase::AwaitingImplement => /* send implementer, settle, pri_after_implement → phase,
                                           continue */
        PriPhase::AwaitingVerify   => /* send verify prompt to reviewer, settle, harvest, parse,
                                         pri_route(...) → continue */
        PriPhase::Done            => { println!("VERIFIED (paper-first)"); return Ok(()); }
        PriPhase::Escalated       => { eprintln!("escalate: ..."); return Ok(()); }
    };
}
```

Keep the existing pure helpers unchanged — they are correct: `pri_route` (~5064),
`pri_after_plan` (~5164), `pri_after_implement` (~5149), `parse_review_token` (~4991),
`extract_plan_path` (~5179), `pri_planner_prompt` (~5048). Delete the duplicated inline branches
(the `PromptPlanner` arm currently inlines a full second review cycle; the `PromptReviewer` arm
inlines the implement→verify sequence). The phase variable must be READ each iteration (fixes the
dead-assignment warnings). Keep the build-slot-cargo + paper-first language in the prompts
(already in `pri_route`). Remove the `unreachable!()` matches — handle the (impossible) other
case with a `bail!` (or `Escalate`) instead of a panic.

## Success criteria

- `cargo clippy --workspace` clean (no `never_loop`, no dead `phase` assignments, no
  `unreachable!()`).
- `--max-change-rounds 2` genuinely allows two planner↔reviewer CHANGES cycles before escalating.
- A third CHANGES (rounds exhausted) escalates with the documented message, not a bail.
- APPROVE → implement → verify → VERIFIED path unchanged; REJECT at plan or verify escalates.
- E2E: scripted reviewer replies "CHANGES: fix A" then "APPROVE" → planner prompted twice, gate
  reaches VERIFIED. Scripted "CHANGES" ×3 with max_change_rounds=2 → Escalate
  ("change rounds exhausted").

## Test plan

- Unit: drive the LOOP, not just `pri_route`. Refactor the loop body into a testable pure
  function that takes `&[ReviewToken]` (the scripted reviewer replies) + send/harvest/settle
  closures, OR keep the loop in a helper accepting closures for `send`/`harvest`/`settle`.
  Table-driven: (tokens sequence, max_change_rounds) → visited phases + final outcome
  (VERIFIED | Escalate-with-reason). This is the test that would have caught the bug.
- E2E (live): as in success criteria, with herdr + agent-mail up and scripted agents.
- Keep `pri_route` unit tests green (unchanged pure logic).

## Considerations

- Do NOT change the Resonate workflow topology (`swarm_loop`) — this is the CLI-side pattern
  driver, separate from the durable loop.
- `current_path` (plan file) must survive the loop — each planner revision may update the path;
  keep it in loop scope and pass to prompts.
- CLI surface identical: `flywheel plan-review <project> <feature> --max-change-rounds N
  --planner X --reviewer Y --implementer Z --bead id`.
- **Settle timeout**: `settle_agent` waits up to `1_800_000` ms (30 min) per agent. For a CLI
  gate this is extreme; consider a shorter gate-specific settle (e.g. a `--settle-timeout-ms`
  flag or reuse the loop's confirm_timeout) so a missing agent fails fast. NOTE: do not change
  the durable loop's settle semantics — only the CLI pattern driver's. If added, document the
  default (keep 30 min or pick 5 min; decide in review).
- Depends on F1 (harvest body) — without it the harvested reviewer body is a subject line and
  the token never parses; fix F1 first or in the same PR.

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `src/main.rs` cmd_plan_review (~5200-5480), PriPhase/PriAction (~5028-5047),
pri_route (~5064), pri_after_plan/pri_after_implement (~5149-5175), parse_review_token (~4991),
settle_agent (~5504). ADR-0001 §9.2 defines the pattern. The pure routing is correct; only the
driver loop is broken.
close_reason: evidence: cmd_plan_review rewritten as phase-driven state machine (src/main.rs) — loop routes on current phase each iteration, phase is read (no dead assignments), max_change_rounds honored for any N, unreachable!() removed, inline duplicated branches deleted. clippy never_loop error GONE (0 errors). New tests: plan_review_gate_loops_on_changes_then_verifies (2 review visits, change_rounds=1, HaltVerified), plan_review_gate_escalates_when_change_rounds_exhausted (3 CHANGES with max 2 → Escalated). 254 lib tests pass, e2e 6, parity 2, fmt clean.

title: F3: xproj send --to-project is dead — wire cross-project targeting or remove flag
description:
# F3: xproj send --to-project is dead — wire cross-project targeting (or document + remove)

## Type / priority

bug, P1 (documented cross-project fan-out doesn't do what it claims)

## Background

`flywheel xproj send <project> --to <agent> --to-project <path> --recipe <r> --workers N` is the
cross-project swarm fan-out primitive (ADR-0001 §9.5, AGENTS.md:123). In `src/main.rs` the
`XprojCmd::Send` arm (~line 3110) destructures `to_project` and **never uses it** — clippy flags
`unused variable: to_project` at `src/main.rs:3117`. The send goes to the LOCAL project key
(`project_dir(cfg, project)`) only, addressed to the mapped recipient identity. `to_project`
(the target project the recipient lives in) is silently dropped.

Contrast: `request_contact` DOES support cross-project — `Mail::request_contact`
(`src/mail.rs:385-401`) passes `to_project` through to the agent-mail tool when set, and the
`XprojCmd::Request` arm uses it (`src/main.rs:~3100`). So the contact half of cross-project is
wired; the SEND half is not.

The receive side: the durable loop runs `__xproj-inbox` on the RECEIVER's project key
(`params.project`) and reads `include_bodies: true` — so the pattern only works if the message
lands in the receiver's project archive. With `to_project` dropped, delivery depends on
agent-mail's `send_message` routing by recipient-name across projects — unverified.

## Technical approach

Investigate agent-mail's cross-project delivery semantics first (the MCP server's
`send_message` envelope; check whether recipient-name delivery crosses project boundaries when a
contact link is approved, or whether the message must be sent with the receiver's project_key).
Then pick ONE:

- **(a) Wire it**: if agent-mail supports explicit cross-project addressing, add an optional
  `to_project: Option<&str>` param to `Mail::send` (mirroring `request_contact`'s pattern at
  mail.rs:399) and pass it from `XprojCmd::Send`. Verify the message is delivered into the target
  project's archive so the receiver's `__xproj-inbox` finds it.
- **(b) Resolve-and-register**: if delivery is name-based only, ensure the recipient identity is
  registered in BOTH projects (register-on-spawn already does this per-project; cross-project
  needs the recipient registered in the sender's project too) — then document that `to_project`
  is advisory (contact/product context), and use it for the product/contact hint so the flag
  isn't dead.
- **(c) Remove the flag**: if it cannot be honored, remove `--to-project` from the CLI and
  AGENTS.md, and fail loudly when a user passes it (unknown-arg error), not silently.

Do NOT ship a silently-ignored flag: that is the current bug.

## Success criteria

- No `unused variable: to_project` warning.
- AGENTS.md + README cross-project docs match the implemented behavior.
- EITHER a real cross-project delivery is verified live (message appears in receiver's inbox),
  OR the flag is removed/honest and the receive-loop contract is documented accordingly.
- `xproj parse` contract unchanged (it is the receiver side and works).

## Test plan

- Unit: if `Mail::send` gains a `to_project` param, test the JSON args include it when set
  (mirror `request_contact`'s existing test shape).
- E2E (`tests/collab_patterns_e2e.rs`, live mail): two projects (or one project with two
  identities), `xproj send` with `--to-project`, assert the message is retrievable via
  `__xproj-inbox` on the target project (i.e., the receive loop would see it). This is the
  cross-project e2e the current suite lacks (the existing test only parses `xproj parse`).
- E2E negative: `xproj send` without `--to-project` behaves per the chosen semantics (either
  local-project delivery or a clear error).

## Considerations

- Cross-project contact requires `request_contact`/`respond_contact` approval (agent-mail
  default policy `auto`) — the e2e must ensure the recipient accepts or policy allows delivery.
- The receive side (`cmd_internal_xproj_spawn`, `__xproj-inbox`) is already implemented and
  soft-fails; do not regress it.
- Do not conflate `product` (already sent in the body) with `to_project` — product links group
  projects for unified search; `to_project` is about where the message must land.
- Depends on nothing structurally, but the cross-project e2e in F9's live suite exercises it.

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `src/main.rs` XprojCmd::Send arm (~3110-3150), `Mail::send` (`src/mail.rs:254`),
`Mail::request_contact` with to_project (`src/mail.rs:385-401`), `__xproj-inbox`/`__xproj-spawn`
leaves, `resolve_mail_target` (~1964). AGENTS.md §Runtime fan-out documents the intended flow.
The flag currently parses, prints in JSON, and is ignored.
close_reason: evidence: verified agent-mail send_message has NO to_project param (delivery is name-based; cross-project authorization lives in request_contact to_project, already wired in XprojCmd::Request). Chose option (b): to_project is now routing CONTEXT, not silently dropped — validated (warning if not a dir), carried as to_project=<path> in the body, surfaced in JSON output, unused-var warning gone. New test parse_xproj_request_tolerates_to_project_line. 256 lib tests pass, clippy 0 errors, fmt clean.

title: F4: T3 escalation must actually halt the loop (bounded halt in Blocked arm)
description:
# F4: T3 escalation must actually halt the loop — implement the bounded halt in the Blocked arm

## Type / priority

bug, P1 (documented safety contract not implemented)

## Background

ADR-0001 §4.4 / Phase 4 and the `EscalationTier` docstring (`src/durable.rs:568`) define:

> T3 (+8×interval): loop halts (bounded), final "needs human" mail.

The bead close-reason for bd-blocked-escalation-protocol-8cc also claims "T3 halt-bounded". The
implementation does NOT halt:

- `LoopAction::Blocked` arm (`src/durable.rs:1922-1970`) computes the tier via
  `escalation_tier(first_blocked_ts, now, interval_secs)` and calls `notify_blocked` — nothing
  else. No `return`, no break, no halt. (Verified: the only `EscalationTier::T3` matches in the
  file are the enum + tier fn; the loop arm has no tier-3 branch.)
- `--on-blocked stop` halts at ANY tier (T0!) — a different semantic (immediate stop), not the
  bounded T3 halt.
- `--on-blocked mail` (the default the escalation protocol assumes) NEVER halts: the loop keeps
  polling, keeps re-notifying at T3 every iteration, forever. The T3 mail body even says
  "The swarm loop is halting because this agent stayed blocked past the escalation budget" — a lie.

Net effect: a permanently-blocked agent under `--on-blocked mail` produces unbounded repeated
T3 mail spam and the loop never exits (blocked keeps `all_settled` false and the queue stuck).

## Technical approach

In the `LoopAction::Blocked` arm (`src/durable.rs:~1922`), after computing `tier`, when
`tier == 3` (EscalationTier::T3) and `params.on_blocked == "mail"`, send the T3 notify (existing
path) and then **halt the loop** with a bounded outcome, mirroring the `--on-blocked stop` exit
shape:

```rust
if tier == 3 {
    // send final mail first, then halt
    ctx.run(notify_blocked, NotifyArgs{ tier: 3, .. }).await?;
    return Ok(format!(
        "halted: agent {name} blocked past escalation budget (T3) — human required"
    ));
}
```

Keep T0/T1/T2 as notify-and-continue. Ensure the halt result is distinguishable from normal
"complete" in the CLI output (`flywheel loop` prints it) and in the event log (add a
`state::log_event(EventKind::Loop, { status: "halted", tier: 3, name })` before returning).
Decide the smallest consistent rule and document it:
- `mail` mode: T3 halts (bounded — this bead)
- `stop` mode: halts at T0 (unchanged, existing behavior)
- `continue` mode: never halts (unchanged)

## Success criteria

- `--on-blocked mail` with a permanently blocked agent: T0 ping, T1 re-ping, T2 urgent, T3 final
  mail, then the loop EXITS with a clear "halted ... T3" message. No further T3 mail repeats.
- `--on-blocked stop` still halts at T0 (unchanged).
- `--on-blocked continue` still ignores blockers (unchanged).
- The halt is logged to the event log with tier + agent name.
- Test: table-driven `escalation_tier` (already exists) PLUS a loop-level test asserting the T3
  halt path returns the halted outcome.

## Test plan

- Unit (`src/durable.rs` tests): `blocked_t3_halts_loop` — factor the halt decision into a pure
  fn `on_blocked_tier_exit(tier, on_blocked) -> Option<String>` and test it: tier 3 + mail →
  Some(halt message); tier 0/1/2 + mail → None; any tier + stop → Some (existing behavior); any +
  continue → None.
- E2E (live): block an agent (or script a fake blocked status), run the durable loop with
  `--on-blocked mail` and a short interval; assert the loop terminates with "halted" within the
  bounded window and that exactly one T3 mail was sent.

## Considerations

- The escalation docstring (`src/durable.rs:568`) and AGENTS.md must be updated to state the
  implemented rule (mail→T3 halt; stop→T0 halt; continue→no halt) so future readers trust the
  contract. (F10 docs bead covers the sweep; this bead owns the docstring.)
- Idempotency: the T3 halt uses the SAME `notify_blocked` leaf as the tiers — no new leaf needed.
- Resonate determinism: the return value is a workflow result (string), checkpointed like
  "complete"; crash-resume of a halted loop re-runs and re-halts consistently (first_blocked_ts
  is persisted in loops.json).
- Timing note: `escalation_tier` uses `params.interval_secs` (the BASE interval), but the loop's
  actual cadence is adaptive (`wait_secs` shrinks when events fire). Tier thresholds are therefore
  approximate under load — acceptable (documented in the fn), do not "fix" by coupling to the
  adaptive wait.
- Depends on nothing structural; pair with F10 for the docs wording.

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `src/durable.rs` — `EscalationTier` (~574), `escalation_tier` (~584),
`LoopAction::Blocked` arm (~1922), `notify_blocked` leaf (~775), `all_settled` (~1146).
ADR-0001 §4.4/Phase 4. The loop currently NEVER halts under `--on-blocked mail` regardless of
tier.
close_reason: evidence: on_blocked_tier_exit pure fn (durable.rs) implements mail→T3 halt / stop→T0 / continue→never; Blocked arm sends T3 mail then returns Ok(halted) + logs EventKind::Loop status=halted tier name. Test: blocked_t3_halts_loop_mail_mode_only (full table). 255 lib + 6 e2e + 2 parity green, clippy 0 errors, fmt clean.

title: F5: __xproj-spawn creates FOCUSED workspace — durable loop steals terminal focus
description:
# F5: __xproj-spawn creates a FOCUSED workspace — durable loop steals terminal focus

## Type / priority

bug, P2 (UX defect in overnight durable operation; trivial fix — quick win)

## Background

`cmd_internal_xproj_spawn` (`src/main.rs:6232`) is the durable-loop leaf that spawns the swarm
for a received `[xproj]` cross-project request. It calls:

```rust
cmd_spawn(cfg, project, &AgentCounts{ oc: Some(workers.max(1)), .. }, Some(recipe), &[],
          None,
          false, // background workspace   ← WRONG
          false) // not peer-aware
```

`cmd_spawn`'s 7th parameter is `no_focus: bool`. Passing `false` → `!no_focus = true` →
`workspace_create(Some(dir), Some(label), focus=true)` (`src/main.rs:1500`). A FOCUSED
workspace is created, which **steals the user's terminal focus**. This runs inside the durable
monitoring loop — potentially overnight, unattended — so an incoming cross-project request
yanks the user's cursor into a new workspace.

The comment `// background workspace` documents the INTENT (background, non-focusing) — the
argument contradicts it. This is a plain inverted-boolean blunder.

## Technical approach

Change the call to pass `true` for `no_focus`:

```rust
true,  // background workspace (no focus steal)
```

Verify `cmd_spawn`'s `no_focus` path is exercised: `workspace_create(..., !no_focus)` and the
`println!` branch (`no_focus` → "created (background)"). Optionally harden against this class of
bug: `cmd_spawn` has ~4 positional booleans; consider a small struct/enum for the
focus+peer flags — but that is a refactor with many call sites; the minimal fix is the boolean
flip. If the refactor is done, update all call sites (`cmd_internal_xproj_spawn` ~6232, the CLI
`spawn` handler ~1100) and add a test.

## Success criteria

- `cmd_internal_xproj_spawn` passes `no_focus=true`.
- After a live xproj-triggered spawn, the current focused workspace is UNCHANGED (no focus
  steal) — verify by snapshotting the focused workspace before/after.
- No clippy warnings introduced.

## Test plan

- Unit: if refactored to named flags, a compile-time guarantee (type system). Otherwise, add a
  verify-script grep guard (F9): assert `cmd_internal_xproj_spawn` passes `true` for the no_focus
  position (e.g. grep for `true, // background workspace` or a named-flag marker).
- E2E (live, optional): trigger an xproj spawn from a second project; assert the original
  workspace stays focused.

## Considerations

- This is the durable-loop leaf — the CLI `spawn` command intentionally focuses by default; only
  the loop leaf should be background. Do not change the CLI's focus behavior.
- The bug is a symptom of positional booleans; note it in AGENTS.md coding-philosophy (explicit
  over implicit) so future code uses named params/structs.
- Quick win: one-line fix, no dependency on other beads; can be done in parallel with F1.

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `src/main.rs:6220-6240` (the xproj spawn call), `cmd_spawn` signature ~1477,
`workspace_create` focus logic ~1500. AGENTS.md §Runtime fan-out (the loop spawns swarms for
`[xproj]` requests — must not disturb the operator).
close_reason: evidence: cmd_internal_xproj_spawn now passes no_focus=true (src/main.rs:6183) — durable loop leaf spawns background workspace, no focus steal. CLI spawn paths (1102/3545/3609/3701) unchanged (user-invoked, focus intentionally). Build 0 errors, 255 lib tests pass.

title: F6: ADR-0002 call-site migration partial — finish or amend ADR; fix verify-0002 check
description:
# F6: ADR-0002 call-site migration is partial — finish it or amend the ADR; fix verify-0002's check

## Type / priority

feature + bug, P1 (ADR compliance honesty)

## Background

ADR-0002 §3.1/R0 mandates: "migrate call sites to `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>` +
`Box<dyn MailBackend>` from the factory, not concrete `Client`/`Mail`. The loop holds trait
objects." The review measured the reality:

- `cmd_internal_send` (`__send` leaf, `src/main.rs:5862`) still uses concrete
  `Client::connect` — its confirm-path uses `Client::agent_prompt_coded` (typed HerdrError →
  landing semantics) which the trait surface does not expose. Verified:
  `agent_prompt_coded` exists at `src/herdr.rs:990` but the trait `MultiplexerBackend::agent_prompt`
  (`src/backend/mod.rs:219`) only exposes the plain variant. The bead close
  (bd-call-site-migration-s1j) honestly deferred this: "DESIGN QUESTION DEFERRED".
- ~20 more concrete `Client::connect` sites remain in `src/main.rs` (spawn, watch, serve, mail
  commands, etc.).
- 5 `mail::Mail::from_config` sites remain (xproj inbox, mail CLI, etc.).
- **verify-0002.sh's check is self-inconsistent**: it greps
  `'Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>' src/main.rs src/durable.rs` — which matches NOTHING because the
  code uses `backend::multiplexer_backend(cfg)` (factory) and local `let mut backend = ...`
  bindings — yet the script PASSES (WARN only). So the gate neither confirms migration nor
  honestly reports the gap.

This is an honesty defect: the verification script and the code disagree about what "migrated"
means, and the ADR's R0 "zero behavior change, all call sites" is not true.

## Technical approach

Two sub-decisions, both must be made EXPLICITLY (not left to future inference):

### A. Finish or formally defer the remaining call sites

Option (a) — finish: extend the `MultiplexerBackend` trait with a coded-prompt method
(`agent_prompt_coded(target, text, wait) -> Result<PromptResult>` where PromptResult carries the
coded error — port `HerdrError` landing semantics onto the trait's `PromptResult` type), so
`cmd_internal_send` can route through the factory. This is the "right" end-state per ADR-0002
(the loop is backend-agnostic; superlogical/toron swap must include send-landing semantics).
Cost: trait + HerdrBackend impl + stub defaults (`Unsupported`) for the other backends + parity
test asserting landing semantics (working/blocked/deduped) match the concrete path.

Option (b) — formal defer: document in ADR-0002 (amendment) that `__send`'s landing-detection
remains concrete until the trait gains a coded-prompt method, and mark the deferred sites with a
`// TODO(ADR-0002): migrate` + reference to THIS bead. Keep the deferral visible, not implicit.

Recommendation: (a) for `cmd_internal_send` (it is the load-bearing leaf for the durable loop's
dispatch correctness), and a sweep to route the remaining `Client::connect` sites through the
factory where the trait already covers the operation (workspace create/list, pane split, agent
start — all present in the trait). `mail::Mail::from_config` sites should move to
`backend::mail_backend(cfg)`.

### B. Fix verify-0002.sh

Replace the literal `'Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>'` grep with checks that match reality:

```bash
# (a) factory exists and returns trait objects
grep -rq '-> Result<Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>>' src/backend/factory.rs
# (b) the durable-loop leaves route through the factory (not concrete Client::connect)
! grep -n 'Client::connect' src/durable.rs | grep -v '^#'   # leaves shell to the binary; assert no concrete in durable.rs
# (c) remaining concrete sites in main.rs are ONLY the documented deferrals
#     (e.g. count them and fail if the count grows)
```

Make the check fail on regression (concrete sites > documented baseline) instead of WARN.

## Success criteria

- Either (a) `cmd_internal_send` routes through the factory, or (b) ADR-0002 is amended with an
  explicit deferral note and the code has `// TODO(ADR-0002)` markers.
- All straightforward call sites (workspace/pane/agent ops the trait already covers) use the
  factory.
- verify-0002.sh: (1) passes with the real check, (2) FAILS when a new concrete `Client::connect`
  appears in durable.rs, (3) counts/limits main.rs concrete sites.
- `cargo test` green, clippy clean, no behavior change (parity: trait-routed == direct, per the
  existing `backend::parity` module which must stay green).

## Test plan

- Unit: `backend::parity` tests already prove trait==direct for the migrated ops; add parity for
  `agent_prompt_coded` if the trait gains it.
- Gate: run verify-0002.sh before/after; assert it FAILS on a deliberately reintroduced concrete
  call (temporarily), then passes.
- E2E: `__send` confirm-path still lands prompts correctly (live herdr) after migration.

## Considerations

- `cmd_internal_send`'s confirm path (`agent_prompt_coded`) is the ONE genuinely hard case — the
  trait's `agent_prompt` returns minimal JSON losing the coded error. The parity test for it must
  assert landing semantics (working/blocked/deduped) match the concrete path byte-for-byte.
- Do not let this balloon: the goal is honest ADR compliance + a gate that detects drift, not a
  full generic-ification of every CLI command (CLI commands may legitimately stay concrete if
  the trait doesn't cover them — but then the ADR must say so).
- Depends on nothing; blocks the verify-script honesty (F9) and the docs bead (F10).

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `src/backend/factory.rs` (multiplexer_backend/mail_backend), `src/backend/mod.rs`
(traits, agent_prompt ~219), `src/backend/parity.rs` (differential tests), `src/herdr.rs`
(agent_prompt_coded ~990), `src/main.rs` (cmd_internal_send ~5862, ~20 concrete Client::connect
sites), `docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0002.sh`. ADR-0002 §3.1/R0.
close_reason: evidence: durable-loop leaf surface FULLY factory-routed — __send (via new trait agent_prompt_coded with PromptLanding status-XOR-code), __kind, __read, __respawn (via start_agent_with_retry_dyn), __xproj-inbox. Trait gained agent_prompt_coded + MailBackend::agent_name. ADR-0002 amended with explicit CLI deferral (interactive commands stay concrete — operation-shaped trait is loop-scoped). verify-0002.sh rewritten to check real behavior (factory returns trait objects, no Client::connect in durable.rs, agent_prompt_coded wired, main.rs concrete ≤30) and PASSES. New test prompt_landing_maps_landed_status_and_coded_error. 257 lib + 6 e2e + 2 parity green, clippy 0 errors, fmt clean, verify-0001+0002 pass.

title: F7: debate/plan-review default agents don't resolve — make defaults work against spawned swarms
description:
# F7: debate/plan-review default agents don't resolve — make defaults work against spawned swarms

## Type / priority

bug, P2 (defaults silently fail; user must pass explicit names every time)

## Background

- `cmd_debate`/`resolve_debate_agents` (`src/main.rs:~5487`) default to `a="oc"`, `b="pi"`,
  `j="gk"` (bare kind shorts).
- `cmd_plan_review` defaults to `planner="oc"`, `reviewer="pi"`, `implementer="gk"`.
- But spawned agents are named `flywheel-<base>-<short>` (e.g. `flywheel-hachiko-oc`) by
  `agent_name_n` (`src/main.rs:~1608`), and the FIRST agent of a kind is `flywheel-<base>-oc`
  (no ordinal suffix). (`agent_ordinal` parses `flywheel-<base>-<short><ordinal>`; `--to oc`
  works via prefix matching in `name_matches_want`.)

Three resolution paths break with bare shorts:

1. **settle path**: `settle_agent(mux, "oc")` → `mux.agent_wait("oc", ...)` → herdr `agent.wait
   target="oc"` — herdr agents are named `flywheel-<base>-oc`, so "oc" does NOT resolve (unless
   herdr fuzzy-matches; the e2e "may fail settle" tolerance hides this).
2. **mail path**: `resolve_mail_target("oc")` → `"oc"` (no hyphen → passthrough, per
   `resolve_mail_target` ~1964). But `register_spawned_agent` registered the agent under the
   MAPPED adjective+noun identity (e.g. `TopazOx`), NOT `oc`. So mail to `"oc"` is an
   unregistered recipient → `send_message` fails fast.
3. **poll path**: the loop's `resolve_agents_dyn` (used by `__poll`) DOES expand shorts via
   `agent_name(project, short)` + prefix matching — so the loop works with shorts, but the
   pattern drivers (`debate`/`plan-review`) use the raw settle/mail paths.

Net: `flywheel debate "X"` with defaults (the documented one-liner) fails unless the user
pre-creates identities named exactly `oc`/`pi`/`gk`. The e2e tests tolerate this, so it ships.

## Technical approach

Make the pattern drivers resolve defaults through the same expansion the loop uses:

- Add a helper `resolve_agent_default(project, short) -> String` that maps a bare kind short to
  the spawned name `agent_name_n(project, short, 1)` — but ONLY when the short doesn't already
  look like a concrete agent name (a herdr name with a `flywheel-` prefix or a valid
  adjective+noun pair passes through). Reuse `valid_pair`/`agent_mail_name` logic for the
  pass-through test.
- In `cmd_debate` and `cmd_plan_review`: resolve defaults (and explicit args) through this
  helper for BOTH the herdr settle path (use the full `flywheel-<base>-<short>` name) and the
  mail path (`resolve_mail_target` already maps the full name correctly).
- Keep the CLI surface identical; defaults just become actually-functional.
- Edge: if the swarm was spawned with a different label/base (e.g. `--label` override or a
  manually-named agent), the helper should fall back gracefully: try the expanded name; if the
  agent isn't found at settle time, surface a clear error listing available agents (the
  `resolve_agents_dyn` error already does this for the poll path — reuse its message shape).

## Success criteria

- `flywheel debate "prop"` with defaults works against a freshly spawned default swarm
  (spawn oc+pi+gk → debate resolves the three real agents → three distinct agents, mail reaches
  registered identities).
- `flywheel plan-review <proj> <feat>` with defaults reaches the planner without "agent not
  found" / "unknown recipient".
- Explicit full names (`--agent-a flywheel-hachiko-oc2`) still pass through unchanged.
- No regression in `resolve_agents_dyn` / the loop's `--to oc` behavior.

## Test plan

- Unit: `resolve_agent_default` table test — bare shorts expand to `flywheel-<base>-<short>`;
  `flywheel-*` and adjective+noun names pass through; empty → error or passthrough per contract.
- E2E (live): debate with defaults against a spawned swarm → assert all three settle + all three
  mail deliveries succeed (mail.send ok) and the verdict prints.
- E2E (live): plan-review with defaults → planner prompt lands.

## Considerations

- Do NOT change `agent_name_n` naming scheme (the loop + `--to` prefix matching depend on it).
- The adjective+noun mapping (bd-odc) is the addressable identity; never send mail to a bare
  short unless a real identity with that name exists — `resolve_mail_target` handles it, but the
  DEFAULT should produce the mapped identity, which requires the full herdr name as input.
- This is a UX-correctness bead: it makes the documented one-liners work. Keep scope tight —
  no redesign of agent naming.
- **Ordering dependency on F1 (soft, kept as a hard edge for sequencing):** F1 fixes WHAT
  content is harvested; F7 fixes WHO is addressed. Technically independent, but both feed the
  same live debate e2e — F1 first so the F7 e2e can assert content + addressing together.
  The `F7 → F1` dependency edge is retained for sequencing (shared e2e), not because F7's code
  requires F1's.

## Self-contained reminder

Relevant code: `resolve_debate_agents` (~5487), `cmd_plan_review` defaults (~5210),
`agent_name_n`/`agent_name` (~1608, ~2430), `resolve_mail_target` (~1964), `valid_pair`/ADJECTIVES
(~1700), `resolve_agents_dyn` (~973), `settle_agent` (~5504). ADR-0001 §9.1/§9.2 patterns.

Debate loop refactored to &str refs, dead opponent var removed. Tests: resolve_agent_default_expands_shorts_and_passes_concrete, debate_resolves_default_agents (now asserts spawned name), debate_accepts_explicit_agents, debate_rejects_same_agent. 258 lib + 6 e2e + 2 parity green, clippy 0 errors, fmt clean.

title: F8: dead legacy code + clippy warning cleanup (track_unknown, SelfHeal, debate dead var, too_many_arguments)
