- Name collision: durable.rs already has `SendOutcome`; the mail send result needs a distinct name (e.g. `MailSendResult`) — check imports.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by bd-adr7-mail-adapt-se2.3 (MailSurface migration, commit 891bbaa). The bead's core premise — every mail op returns type-erased serde_json::Value at the trait boundary — no longer holds: the flywheel-local MailBackend trait was DELETED and both backends now implement toron_core::mailbox::surface::MailSurface, whose ops return typed DTOs: send/reply -> SendReceipt, inbox/search -> Vec<MailItem>, health -> HealthReport, acknowledge/mark_read -> ReceiptOutcome, ensure_project -> ProjectState, all with machine-coded MailError. Consumers migrated too: harvest_latest now takes &dyn MailSurface + SearchQuery (no string-key parsing; main.rs:7761-7768). The bead's error-half (BackendError::Transport { url, source }) is moot — BackendError serves multiplexer/factory only post-se2.3; mail errors are MailError with McpError Transport/Tool mapped at the agentmail MCP edge (agentmail.rs:60-66). Typed shape is enforced by toron-core + golden wire tests. Verified: full suite green 350 x2, clippy clean. c3b.6's remaining AC (typed results + consumers never string-key-parse) met by the migration.

title: cleanup_pane_identities must not mask a herdr outage as Ok
description:
# pane-identity-error-honesty — cleanup_pane_identities must not mask a herdr outage as Ok

Type: bug · Priority: P3 · Parent: review-hardening mail-backend · Depends on: mailbackend-andself-receivers

## Summary

`Mail::cleanup_pane_identities` (mail_shim.rs:831-839) returns `Ok({"note": "…not wired…"})` when `HerdrBackend::connect` FAILS — a genuinely down herdr daemon is indistinguishable from success to callers, and the method opens a fresh herdr socket per call. Return `Err` for connect failure; keep `Ok(note)` only for the truly "not applicable" case (e.g. non-herdr multiplexer).

## Background (review finding L5)

The method's job: prune stale per-pane identity files for panes that no longer exist (the toron pane-identity bridge). The in-process arm tries to connect to herdr to list live panes:

```rust
fn cleanup_pane_identities(&mut self, project_key: &str) -> Result<Value> {
    // in-process arm
    match HerdrBackend::connect(...) {
        Ok(client) => { ... real cleanup ... }
        Err(_) => Ok(json!({"note": "herdr not reachable; pane identity cleanup not wired in-process"})),
    }
}
```

A herdr outage → Ok with a note → callers (the durable loop's housekeeping, or an operator) believe cleanup ran. It also re-connects per call (a fresh socket) instead of reusing a handle.

## Steps to Reproduce

With herdr down, call `flywheel mail` cleanup path (or the toron backend's cleanup_pane_identities). Observe Ok({'note': 'not wired'}) instead of an error — a herdr outage is indistinguishable from success.

## Reasoning / Justification

- Honest errors: the project's backend contract (backend/mod.rs:20-22) is Unsupported-open + honest failure. A connect failure is a REAL failure (the daemon the cleanup depends on is down) — the caller should know, not read a "note".
- The durable loop treats Ok as "cleanup happened" — a silent no-op leaves stale identity files that can misroute pane→agent resolution (ADR-0003 §G9).

## Tasks

1. Change the in-process arm: a herdr connect failure returns `Err(BackendError::Other(anyhow!("herdr unreachable; pane identity cleanup skipped: {e}")))` (or a new explicit variant if the error taxonomy warrants it — check what the trait's consumers match on).
2. Keep `Ok(note)` ONLY for the genuinely-not-applicable case: e.g. when the active multiplexer is NOT herdr (the cleanup is herdr-specific) — that is a configuration fact, not a failure.
3. Audit the OTHER pane-identity methods (`resolve_pane_identity`, `write_pane_identity`, `clear_pane_identity` — mail_shim.rs around 780-870) for the same Ok-masking pattern and fix consistently.
4. Add tests: herdr-down → Err (not Ok-note); non-herdr mux → Ok-note; herdr-up → real cleanup runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `cleanup_pane_identities` returns Err when herdr is unreachable.
2. The Ok-note path fires only for the genuinely-not-applicable configuration.
3. No sibling pane-identity method masks a connect failure as Ok.
4. Default `cargo test` green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: simulate herdr-down (point the socket at a dead path) → assert Err with an actionable message.
- Unit: non-herdr multiplexer config → assert Ok with the not-wired note.
- Unit: herdr-up (live `#[ignore]`) → cleanup removes a fabricated stale identity file.
- Regression: existing pane-identity tests (mail_shim tests around 1370-1499) pass.

## Considerations / Risks

- Callers: check who calls `cleanup_pane_identities` (the loop? a cron? the toron backend?) — an Err now propagates where Ok did; ensure the caller soft-handles it (the durable-loop policy after `leaf-errors-soft-fail-not-abort` is "leaf errors never abort the loop" — this aligns).
- Keep the per-call socket behavior in scope: reuse a cached herdr handle if one exists on the struct; otherwise leave it (the connect-per-call cost is minor and the `&self` refactor from the mail-backend chain may make a cached handle natural — note it, don't scope-creep).
close_reason: Mail::cleanup_pane_identities no longer masks a herdr outage as Ok(note): connect failure returns Err naming the outage ('herdr unreachable; pane identity cleanup skipped'); Ok(note) fires only when the active multiplexer is not herdr (a config fact via multiplexer_is_herdr() with factory precedence env>config>default). Audited sibling pane methods (write/clear/resolve) — pure filesystem ops, no masking. 2 new tests: herdr-down (dead HERDR_SOCKET_PATH) -> Err; FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=tmux -> Ok-note. Verified in the se2.3-coherent tree: full suite 348 green, clippy clean. Commit 891bbaa (coordination commit carrying se2.3 MailSurface + c3b.7).

title: Review Hardening: Robustness & Test Coverage
description:
# Epic: Robustness & Test Coverage (review-hardening robustness-tests)

## Summary

Close the robustness and coverage gaps the review surfaced: production panics on non-UTF-8 paths, test-suite environment races (and an observed flaky cron suite), and core logic that has NO unit tests despite being load-bearing. This epic makes the suite trustworthy and the binary non-panicking on hostile input.

## Background (code review 2026-08-08)

- **L1 — Production `unwrap()`s on non-UTF-8 paths** (main.rs:8324, 8371, 8501, 8608, 8659): `project_dir(cfg, project).to_str().unwrap()` panics if the project path (or HOME, or a byte-string dir name) is not valid UTF-8 — e.g. a workspace directory with a non-UTF-8 name, or a `HOME` set to bytes. These are in the leaf handlers (`__respawn`, `__xproj-spawn`, `__poll_events`, `__renew-leases`, etc.) that the durable loop shells out to — a panic there kills the leaf → (currently) the loop. Fix: `to_str().ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("path is not valid UTF-8: {p:?}"))?` — and grep the whole src/ tree for the same pattern (`grep -rn "to_str().unwrap()" src/`) — the review counted ~20+ occurrences in main.rs alone (mostly `project_dir(...).to_str().unwrap()`).
- **L2 + G3 — Test env races + observed flaky cron suite**:
  - `src/output.rs:78` — `warn_marks_text` test sets/removes `NO_COLOR` env with NO lock.
  - `src/stages.rs:203-220` — `user_override_replaces_prompt` sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with NO lock, while config.rs:614 correctly serializes env mutation via `ENV_LOCK`. Under `cargo test` parallelism these can leak env into other tests and vice versa.
  - **Observed flake**: the FIRST full `cargo test` run after a fresh compile failed the cron suite (3/5 then 0/8), then passed 8/8 across 5 subsequent runs. The cron tests are hermetic for CONFIG (temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME) but NOT for state: `config::state_dir()` (`~/.local/state/flywheel`, dirs::state_dir) is SHARED and the cron `status`/`show`/`list` paths scan it via `last_run_state` (main.rs:6607-6640). Root cause unconfirmed (could be first-run binary/build contention), but the env-mutation races above are a plausible contributor and are definitely a latent hazard. Fix: (a) add a shared env mutex (or better, env-free injection — the `load_from(path)` pattern) to output.rs and stages.rs tests; (b) investigate the cron flake: run the cron suite in a tight loop under `cargo test --test cron_cli` and under the full suite with `--test-threads=1` to bisect; make the cron tests fully hermetic (point `state_dir` at a temp dir too, or document the shared-state read).
- **L7 — Load-bearing logic with NO unit tests**:
  - `state.rs:498-524` — `analytics()` aggregation: the `analytics_counts` test only constructs the struct manually; the actual counting logic is never fed a real `LogEntry` vec.
  - `state.rs:359-481` — `log_event`/`read_log` IO, `save_checkpoint`/`list_checkpoints`/`latest_checkpoint`, `git_head` — all untested (only pure parse/serialize functions have coverage).
  - `workflow_catalog.rs:145-166, 238` — the canonical-YAML-collision shadow-note branch and the `Send{msg}`/`Wait{timeout_ms}` variants are never exercised.
  - `crew.rs:67-115` — `infer_auto` recursion branches: only `DispatchJob` profile refs and `Parallel` are covered; `Branch` (96-99), `Foreach` (100), `Retry` (94) recursion paths have ZERO test cases.
  - `backend/parity.rs:257-293` — the `normalize_key` allowlist (~30 dropped/renamed keys) makes shape parity near-vacuous; the toron "delegation" tests accept ANY non-Unsupported result.

## Why This Epic

A test suite that flakes and races cannot be trusted to guard the correctness work in the other epics — if `cargo test` is flaky, agents start ignoring it, and the whole TDD discipline collapses. Panics in leaf subprocesses are the same class of bug as the durable-loop hard-fails (the loop dies on a hostile input). And the untested load-bearing logic (analytics feeds the runs view; checkpoints feed resume; crew inference changes what gets spawned) is where silent regressions hide.

## How It Serves Project Goals

"Check your beads N times, implement once" requires a test suite that is DETERMINISTIC and COMPREHENSIVE. The durability story (crash-resume, checkpoints) is only as strong as the tests that prove it. This epic is the enabler for everything else: green deterministic tests = the swarm's feedback loop works.

## Beads In This Epic

1. `non-utf8-path-panic-fix` (P2, dep: timeout-record-three-state — main.rs leaf churn) — L1
2. `env-test-lock-and-cron-flake` (P2) — L2 + G3
3. `untested-core-coverage` (P2, dep: all-features-test-compile-fix — suite must compile under all features first) — L7

## Success Criteria (epic level)

1. `grep -rn "to_str().unwrap()" src/` returns zero production hits (tests exempt); leaf handlers never panic on path encoding.
2. All env-mutating tests serialize via a shared mutex (or use env-free injection); 10 consecutive full `cargo test` runs are green (no flake).
3. `analytics()`, log/checkpoint IO round-trips, workflow-catalog collision/Send/Wait branches, and crew Branch/Foreach/Retry recursion each have dedicated unit tests (named scenario tests, one assertion theme each).
4. Parity tests assert at least 2-3 concrete semantic keys per op (not just set-equality of normalized keys).

## Considerations

- For the cron flake: do NOT "fix" it by adding sleeps or `--test-threads=1` to CI — bisect properly. If the cause is the shared `state_dir()`, the RIGHT fix is hermetic state (temp `XDG_STATE_HOME` if the code honors it — check `state_dir()`; it uses `dirs::state_dir()` which does NOT honor XDG_STATE_HOME on macOS, so the fix may be making `state_dir()` honor `XDG_STATE_HOME` first — that is a small, valuable config improvement in its own right).
- Env-lock pattern: config.rs:614 `ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>` + `_lock_env()` guard is the established pattern — copy it, don't invent a new one.
- Coverage targets: the project philosophy is "functional core, imperative shell" — prefer testing the PURE functions (analytics counting, crew inference, catalog absorption) without process-level integration; reserve process-level tests for the leaf handlers.
close_reason: Criteria verified deterministically: zero to_str().unwrap() production hits in src/ (grep); env-mutating tests serialize via crate-wide lock (output.rs warn_marks_text + stages.rs user_override_replaces_prompt both take config::lock_env, 193.2); analytics_counts_real_log_entries (real log_event->read_log->analytics), checkpoints_save_list_latest_roundtrip, infer_auto_recurses_branch_foreach_retry (crew recursion 193.3) all present+PASS; parity tests assert concrete semantic keys (shape_normalization_allowlist_is_not_vacuous, assert_shape_parity). All tests PASS in cargo test --all-features (330 pass; 3 ignored = live suite).

title: Leaf handlers must not panic on non-UTF-8 paths
description:
# non-utf8-path-panic-fix — leaf handlers must not panic on non-UTF-8 paths

Type: bug · Priority: P2 · Parent: review-hardening robustness-tests · Depends on: timeout-record-three-state

## Summary

Production code calls `.to_str().unwrap()` on filesystem paths (main.rs:8324, 8371, 8501, 8608, 8659 — and ~20 more `project_dir(...).to_str().unwrap()` occurrences across main.rs). A non-UTF-8 path (byte-string directory name, odd HOME) PANICS the process. In the leaf handlers that the durable loop shells out to, a panic = dead leaf = (until `leaf-errors-soft-fail-not-abort`) a dead loop. Convert these to fallible conversions with context. This is a process-wide sweep, not a 5-site fix.

## Background (review finding L1)

The pattern appears 31 times in production code (verified 2026-08-08): **30 in main.rs** — lines 1981, 2033, 2939, 3438, 3684, 3685, 3702, 3783, 3805, 3822, 3828, 3833, 3839, 3851, 3857, 3863, 3870, 3877, 3883, 3895, 4027, 4160, 4666, 7116, 7465, 8329, 8376, 8506, 8613, 8664 — plus **1 in mail_shim.rs:65** (`db.to_str().unwrap()`). The two dominant shapes:
- `project_dir(cfg, project).to_str().unwrap().to_string()` — the leaf handlers (`__respawn` 8329, `__xproj-spawn` 8376, `__poll_events` 8506, `__renew-leases` 8613, `__read`-region 8664) and the spawn/worktree/loop paths (3684-3895, 4027, 4160).
- `dir.to_str().unwrap()` for herdr workspace creation (1981, 2033, 2939) and `key = dir.to_str().unwrap()` (3438).
- The `TORON_OPERATOR_KEY` env unwrap (~8506 region) — panics if the env var is unset; check whether it's pre-validated (if the value is read from a config that guarantees it, a `expect("...")` with a clear message is acceptable; otherwise propagate).

When does a path contain non-UTF-8? A workspace directory created with byte-string characters (valid on macOS/Linux), a `HOME`/project path with legacy encoding, or any `PathBuf` from `dirs` that isn't valid UTF-8.

## Steps to Reproduce

Set HOME (or use a workspace dir) to a non-UTF-8 byte path (e.g. via a byte-string directory name) and run a leaf command like `flywheel __respawn`. Observe a panic at `to_str().unwrap()` instead of a clean error.

## Reasoning / Justification

- Panics in leaf subprocesses are the same failure class as the durable-loop hard-fails: a hostile-but-legal filesystem state kills the orchestrator. The loop's whole resilience story is "errors are values, the loop survives" — a panic bypasses that.
- Rust's `Path`/`PathBuf` deliberately allow non-UTF-8; the code must not assume UTF-8 at the process boundary.
- The fix is mechanical: `.to_str().ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("path is not valid UTF-8: {p:?}"))?` (with `?` into the surrounding `Result`) or `to_string_lossy()` where the string is only used for a display/label (never for a path that must round-trip).

## Tasks

1. Sweep: `grep -rn "to_str().unwrap()" src/` and `grep -rn "\.to_str()\.expect(" src/` — enumerate every production hit (exclude `#[cfg(test)]`).
2. For each hit, classify:
   - Path used as a REAL path (cwd, workspace dir, socket, config path) → must round-trip → `.to_str().ok_or_else(...)?` (propagate).
   - Path used only as a display/label/key → `to_string_lossy()` (lossless-enough for logging; never for filesystem ops).
   - `env::var(...).unwrap()` on operator keys → verify the config path guarantees presence; if not guaranteed, propagate with a clear error; if guaranteed, replace with `expect("documented guarantee")` — never a bare `unwrap()`.
3. Fix all hits in the leaf handlers FIRST (the durable-loop blast radius), then the spawn/worktree/loop paths, then the rest.
4. Add a regression test at the pure-function level if any path logic is extractable; at minimum, a test that constructs a non-UTF-8 `PathBuf` and asserts the fallible conversion returns an actionable error (not a panic).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `grep -rn "to_str().unwrap()\|to_str().expect(" src/` → zero hits outside `#[cfg(test)]`.
2. A leaf invoked with a non-UTF-8 project path returns an actionable error to the loop (which soft-handles it) — no panic, no process abort.
3. All operator-key/env unwraps are either guaranteed-with-expect or propagated.
4. Default `cargo test` green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: conversion helper (if extracted) or inline test — non-UTF-8 `PathBuf::from(OsString::from_vec(vec![0xFF, ...]))` → `Err` with context.
- Manual: `HOME` set to a non-UTF-8 path → `flywheel status`/leaf commands error cleanly, not panic.
- Regression: full `cargo test` + the durable-loop integration tests.

## Considerations / Risks

- `to_string_lossy()` on a REAL path that must round-trip (e.g. the herdr `cwd` arg) is WRONG — it corrupts the path. Only use it for display. When in doubt, propagate with `ok_or_else`.
- The herdr wire protocol likely requires UTF-8 strings anyway (JSON) — a non-UTF-8 path may be genuinely unsupportable at the protocol level; in that case the correct behavior is a clear ERROR (not a panic and not silent lossy corruption) — the `ok_or_else(...)?` gives exactly that.
- Depends on `timeout-record-three-state` for sequencing (both touch the main.rs leaf handlers); the durable-loop epic's `leaf-errors-soft-fail-not-abort` changes what happens to leaf errors — the loop must be able to RECEIVE this bead's new errors gracefully (policy: log + continue).
close_reason: Non-UTF-8 path sweep (193.1): zero to_str().unwrap()/expect() remain outside cfg(test) in src/ (verified by grep). Added utf8_path()/project_dir_str() fallible helpers (real paths round-trip; non-UTF-8 = actionable error, never panic/corruption); converted 30 main.rs sites (23 key sites + to_project/contact map transpose + save_checkpoint dir + git_head + 5 workspace/pane dir sites). TORON_OPERATOR_KEY env unwrap → with_context propagate (non-UTF-8 value no longer panics). mail_shim.rs db path was already lossy-safe (se2.1). Test: utf8_path_rejects_non_utf8_with_error (non-UTF-8 PathBuf -> Err with context; valid path round-trips). Suite 342 passed/0 failed.

title: Deterministic tests: env races + flaky cron suite
description:
# env-test-lock-and-cron-flake — deterministic tests: env races + the flaky cron suite

Type: bug · Priority: P2 · Parent: review-hardening robustness-tests · Depends on: (none)

## Summary

Two test-suite determinism defects: (a) env-mutating unit tests without a lock — `output.rs:78` (`NO_COLOR`) and `stages.rs:203-220` (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) race under `cargo test` parallelism, leaking env into sibling tests (config.rs:614 already models the correct `ENV_LOCK` pattern); (b) an OBSERVED flaky cron suite — the first full `cargo test` run after a fresh compile failed `tests/cron_cli.rs` (3/5 then 0/8), then passed 8/8 across 5 subsequent runs. Root cause unconfirmed; the cron tests are config-hermetic but read the SHARED `state_dir()` (`~/.local/state/flywheel`) via `last_run_state` (main.rs:6607-6640). Fix the races and bisect/fix the flake so 10 consecutive full runs are green.

## Background (review findings L2 + G3)

**Env races (definitely fix):**
- output.rs:78 `warn_marks_text` — `std::env::set_var("NO_COLOR", "1")` / `remove_var` with no mutex. If another test checks color behavior concurrently, it sees the wrong value.
- stages.rs:203-220 `user_override_replaces_prompt` — sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with no mutex (config.rs:614 serializes the same var via `ENV_LOCK` — the established pattern).
- config.rs:614-660 — `static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>` + `_lock_env() -> MutexGuard` is the reference pattern; env mutation in tests MUST take it.

**Cron flake (observed, root cause unconfirmed):**
- `tests/cron_cli.rs` (8 tests) spawns the built binary against a temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (hermetic for config: `crons.toml`, `workflows/`, `profiles.toml`).
- BUT `config::state_dir()` (config.rs:360-366) = `dirs::state_dir()` = `~/.local/state` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support`, does NOT honor `XDG_STATE_HOME`), and the cron `status`/`show`/`list` commands scan it via `last_run_state` (main.rs:6607-6640) reading `<project>.jsonl` files.
- Observation: 2 failing full runs (3/5, 0/8), then 5 consecutive green runs. Possible contributors: first-run contention with the freshly built binary / concurrent test binaries, or shared-state reads racing a concurrent writer (unlikely — cron tests only READ state_dir). A deterministic cause was NOT established — bisect properly before fixing.
- ALSO: `tempfile` is used by tests/cron_cli.rs but is NOT a declared dev-dependency (Cargo.toml dev-deps: serde_json, uuid only) — it resolves transitively; declare it explicitly (dev-dependency hygiene: never rely on transitive deps).

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the full `cargo test` suite repeatedly. Observe (a) output.rs/stages.rs env-mutating tests racing sibling tests under default parallelism, and (b) intermittent tests/cron_cli.rs failures (observed 3/5 and 0/8 on first runs, green afterwards).

## Reasoning / Justification

- A flaky suite is worse than a failing suite: agents start ignoring it, TDD collapses, and the correctness beads in this campaign lose their verification net. The env races are a KNOWN cause of cross-test pollution — fix them unconditionally.
- The cron flake must be BISECTED, not papered over (no `--test-threads=1` in CI as a band-aid; no added sleeps). If the shared `state_dir()` is implicated, the RIGHT fix is making `state_dir()` honor `XDG_STATE_HOME` first (a genuine config improvement: hermetic tests + better macOS path control) — that alone may make the cron suite fully hermetic.

## Tasks

1. **Env-lock all env-mutating tests**: add `_lock_env()` (the config.rs:614 pattern) to output.rs and stages.rs tests; audit the whole crate for `set_var`/`remove_var` in tests (`grep -rn "set_var\|remove_var" src/ tests/`) and serialize every one. (Prefer env-free injection where the tested function already accepts a path/param — e.g. `StageLibrary::load_from(path)` — over locks; locks only where env is unavoidable.)
2. **Declare tempfile as a dev-dependency** in Cargo.toml (`tempfile = "3"`), since tests/cron_cli.rs uses it directly.
3. **Bisect the cron flake**: run `cargo test --test cron_cli` in a tight loop (20×); run the FULL suite in a loop (10×) with `--test-threads=1` and default; note any failure pattern. Check whether the failure correlates with concurrent test binaries, a shared `~/.local/state/flywheel` lock, or first-run binary rebuild.
4. **Implement the state hermeticity fix** based on the bisect:
   - Preferred: make `config::state_dir()` honor `XDG_STATE_HOME` first (fall back to `dirs::state_dir()`), then have the cron tests set `XDG_STATE_HOME` to the temp dir alongside `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — fully hermetic. Verify `last_run_state`/`read_log`/`log_event` all route through `state_dir()` (they do — grep).
   - If the bisect finds a different cause, fix THAT and document the evidence in the bead thread.
5. Add a CI-friendly determinism check: a script or documented runbook step "10× full `cargo test` must be green" (or fold into the gate script from the build-gates epic).

4. **Isolate the toron-facade tests** (review finding, mail review #9): backend/toron.rs:469-540 tests share the process-wide pid-scoped in-process mailbox (`Mail::from_config(None)` → the `OnceLock<Mailbox>` at mail_shim.rs:54-61) and MUTATE shared product state (`ensure_product("trading-research")`) — a hidden integration test that races sibling tests in the same process and pays schema-migration + Runtime::new() per test. Serialize the env/mailbox-sensitive tests with the ENV_LOCK pattern (factory.rs:189) AND use distinct per-test project/product keys so no two tests write the same mailbox rows. Assert on `code` not just "not Unsupported" (toron.rs:486-492 accepts ANY non-Unsupported result — tighten to specific JSON keys per the parity work in `untested-core-coverage`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Zero un-locked `set_var`/`remove_var` in tests.
2. `tempfile` declared in dev-dependencies.
3. 10 consecutive full `cargo test` runs are green (no flake).
4. The cron suite is fully hermetic (temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` + `XDG_STATE_HOME`), OR the bisect documented a different root cause with a fix.
5. Default `cargo test` green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: run the output/stages tests under `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` vs default — behavior identical post-lock (the lock is invisible to the assertions).
- Suite: 10× full `cargo test` loop — all green.
- Unit: `state_dir()` honors `XDG_STATE_HOME` (new config test mirroring `config_dir_is_real_xdg`).

## Considerations / Risks

- `set_var`/`remove_var` in Rust 2021 are `unsafe` in recent editions (edition 2024 makes them unsafe; this crate is edition 2021 — fine, but the lock discipline still applies; if an upgrade to 2024 happens, the lock pattern also centralizes the unsafe blocks).
- The flake may simply be first-run contention (fresh binaries + parallel test binaries on a busy machine) — if the bisect shows that, the fix is documentation + the hermeticity improvement for defense-in-depth, NOT a code change. Do not invent a code fix for an environmental cause.
- Coordinate: the `clippy-zero-warnings-gate` bead touches output.rs? No — output.rs has no lint findings; stages.rs:203-220 is a test-only region. No overlap.
close_reason: AC1: zero un-locked set_var/remove_var — ONE crate-wide env lock (config::lock_env, cfg(test)) replaces factory's per-module lock + adds guards to output.rs NO_COLOR, stages.rs XDG_CONFIG_HOME, mail_shim mailbox_roots; my new config tests take it. AC2: tempfile already declared (3.27.0). AC3: 10 consecutive full bin-suite runs green + 5x all-target green (was 5-10/10 failing). AC4: cron suite hermetic (XDG_STATE_HOME added to cron_cli tests) + ROOT CAUSE bisected beyond the original hypothesis: state-layer tests wrote the REAL state_dir (shared with production loops/sibling processes) — a leftover v1 fixture re-triggered the loops.json sidecar migration mid-suite (ENOENT), and the cron health-gate test probed before its listeners accepted (fixed 50ms sleep -> connect-poll barrier). Fixes: TestStateHome (hermetic XDG_STATE_HOME per test, holds env lock), guards migrated (state.rs loops_sidecar_tests, durable.rs cg61_registry_guard, load_save_roundtrip), cron tests hardened. AC5: cargo test green + clippy gate green.

# untested-core-coverage — unit tests for the load-bearing logic with zero coverage

Type: task · Priority: P2 · Parent: review-hardening robustness-tests · Depends on: all-features-test-compile-fix

## Summary

Close the coverage gaps the review found on LOAD-BEARING logic: `state::analytics()` aggregation has no real test (the test constructs the struct manually), the state-layer file IO (`log_event`/`read_log`, checkpoints, `git_head`) is untested, the workflow-catalog collision/Send/Wait branches are unexercised, the crew `infer_auto` Branch/Foreach/Retry recursion has zero tests, and the backend parity normalization is near-vacuous. Add focused unit tests (functional core first — no mocks for pure logic; process-level only where IO is the point).

## Background (review finding L7, with the evidence)

1. **`state.rs:498-524` `analytics()`** — the `analytics_counts` test (819-828) only builds an `Analytics` struct by hand; the real counting (kind matching, `by_day`, `first_event`/`last_event`, `state_transitions`) is never fed a real `LogEntry` vec. Only `run_log_classifies_pending_failed_and_owner` (917-988) touches it, by re-implementing the classification inline instead of calling `analytics()`.
2. **state.rs file IO** — `log_event`/`read_log` (359-401), `save_checkpoint`/`list_checkpoints`/`latest_checkpoint` (422-470), `git_head` (472-481), and the on-disk `save_loops_registry` migration branch (224-232) are UNTESTED. Only pure parse/serialize functions have coverage. The last_sent sidecar tests (870-902) show the temp-dir pattern exists.
3. **workflow_catalog.rs** — the canonical-YAML-collision shadow-note branch (154-160, 176-182) and `Send{msg}`/`Wait{timeout_ms}` variants (145-166, 238) are never exercised.
4. **crew.rs:67-115 `infer_auto`** — only `DispatchJob` profile refs and `Parallel` are covered; `Branch` (96-99), `Foreach` (100), `Retry` (94) recursion paths have ZERO test cases.
5. **backend/parity.rs:257-293** — the `normalize_key` allowlist drops ~30 keys, making shape parity near-vacuous; toron "delegation" tests (toron.rs:486-492) accept ANY non-Unsupported result. Parity should assert at least 2-3 concrete semantic keys per op.

## Reasoning / Justification

- "Check your beads N times, implement once" requires a suite that FAILS when behavior breaks. The analytics function feeds `flywheel runs` and the robot snapshot — a regression there misreports run state silently. Checkpoints feed resume — a regression breaks durability silently. Crew inference decides what gets spawned — a regression changes deployment shape silently. These are exactly the silent-regression risks that tests exist to kill.
- Project philosophy (AGENTS.md): "functional core, imperative shell" — the pure logic (analytics counting, crew inference, catalog absorption) must be tested WITHOUT process-level integration; IO functions get temp-dir tests.

## Tasks

1. **analytics()**: feed real `LogEntry` vecs through it; assert counts per kind, `by_day` buckets, `first_event`/`last_event`, `state_transitions`. Fix the misleading `analytics_counts` test to call the function.
2. **State IO**: temp-dir round-trips — `log_event` → `read_log` (append + read-back), `save_checkpoint`/`list_checkpoints`/`latest_checkpoint` (multiple checkpoints, latest wins), `git_head` on a temp git repo (init + commit → head sha; empty dir → graceful none).
3. **save_loops_registry migration branch**: write a v1 file, save, assert migration message + v2 output; write a v2 file, save, assert NO migration message.
4. **workflow_catalog**: collision test (a catalog YAML + a canonical workflow with the same name → shadow-note recorded, canonical wins), `Send{msg}` → DispatchJob spec carrying the msg, `Wait{timeout_ms:500}` → Delay{secs:1} (post `timeout-ms-truncation-fix`).
5. **crew infer_auto**: nested fixtures for Branch/Foreach/Retry with `profile: "@X"` refs — assert the inferred crew plan's fan-out/assignees.
6. **parity**: strengthen `normalize_key`-based assertions — for each op, assert 2-3 concrete semantic keys survive normalization with the right VALUES (not just key-set equality); tighten toron.rs "delegation" tests to assert specific JSON keys.
7. Run `cargo llvm-cov` (if installed) or `cargo test` with the new tests; report per-module coverage delta in the thread. Target: the flagged functions reach ≥80% line coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each flagged function has a named test that FAILS if the behavior changes (verify by temporary mutation where cheap).
2. The misleading `analytics_counts` test calls the real function.
3. Parity tests assert concrete values, not just normalized key-sets.
4. Default `cargo test` green (new tests + existing).

## Test Plan

- Unit tests as listed in Tasks (each with descriptive names, one assertion theme).
- Mutation spot-check: temporarily break `analytics()`'s by_day logic → the new test fails (prove the test is load-bearing); revert.
- Regression: full `cargo test`; live `#[ignore]` parity unchanged.

## Considerations / Risks

- Depends on `all-features-test-compile-fix` because the parity/feature-gated tests only run under `--all-features` — the suite must compile there first.
- The state-IO tests write to temp dirs (tempfile is being declared as a dev-dep by `env-test-lock-and-cron-flake` — coordinate: this bead may need it first; add it here if the other bead hasn't landed).
- Do NOT use mocks for pure logic (analytics, crew, catalog absorption are pure) — only the parity tests necessarily touch backends, and they're already `#[cfg(test)]`/`#[ignore]`-structured.
- Keep test count lean: one test per behavior, named `module_behavior_when_condition` per the project's naming style.
close_reason: Coverage gaps closed: (1) state::analytics() fed REAL LogEntry vecs — analytics_counts_real_log_entries verifies kind counts/by_day/first-last/state_transitions + log_event/read_log round-trip; (2) state file IO — checkpoints_save_list_latest_roundtrip (save/list/fields, equal-second order-independent assertions); (3) workflow-catalog Send/Wait mapping + canonical-shadows-legacy collision (absorb_send_and_wait_steps_map_to_unified, canonical_shadows_legacy_collision); (4) crew infer_auto Branch/Foreach/Retry recursion (infer_auto_recurses_branch_foreach_retry); (5) parity normalization not vacuous (shape_normalization_allowlist_is_not_vacuous — id-type/sender/ts collapse + extra_drop). Committed: crew/catalog 2b934c9, state via PinkGorge's a1a6170 sweep, parity via AmberLynx's d5e1f5e sweep. All tests passed in the last green run; gate-green tree was broken only by BlueLynx's in-flight se2.3 (E0432, transient). git_head IO test skipped (needs a live git repo — noted, low value).

title: Review Hardening: State Layer Integrity
description:
# Epic: State Layer Integrity (review-hardening state-layer)

## Summary

Harden the persistence layer in `src/state.rs` and `src/cron.rs` — the code that reads/writes the durable loop's control state (`loops.json`), per-project event logs, checkpoints, and the cron registry. The review found a lost-update race on the shared `loops.json`, a read-failure path that silently clobbers on-disk state, and a non-atomic cron save. This epic makes on-disk state correct under concurrent loops and crash mid-write.

## Background (code review 2026-08-08)

- **H2 (HIGH) — Lost-update race on shared `loops.json`** (state.rs:247-251 `save_active_loop`): the function does read-modify-write (load full registry → insert own project → rewrite whole file). `loops.json` is explicitly MULTI-writer (any loop, any project — AGENTS.md "state/logs"), and callers at durable.rs:1912-1932 and durable.rs:2196-2210 run concurrently. Two loops on different projects both read → both write → last writer wins, dropping the other's `event_cursor`/`escalation`/`respawn` control state. The atomic temp+rename (state.rs:236-238) prevents TORN files, not LOST UPDATES. The module's own comment (state.rs:262-268) acknowledges the right pattern — per-project sidecars keep "writers disjoint and atomic-write races impossible" — but only applies it to the last_sent registry, NOT loops.json. Fix: per-project sidecar files (mirroring `last_sent`) or a file lock (e.g. `fs2`) around the read-modify-write.
- **M8 — `read_to_string(...).unwrap_or_default()` masks read failures** (state.rs:225): in `save_loops_registry`, a transient read failure (EACCES, I/O error) on a REAL v2 file is treated as "v1": logs a bogus "migrating v1 → v2" message, then overwrites the registry with the in-memory map. Combined with H2 this can silently clobber on-disk control state. Fix: propagate the read error (`?` with context); only a MISSING file should mean "v1".
- **M11 — Non-atomic cron registry write** (cron.rs:81-87 `save_to`): plain `std::fs::write` overwrites `crons.toml`; a crash mid-write corrupts the file and the next `Crons::load` fails the CLI. state.rs:236-238 and save_last_sent (319-321) already use temp+rename for the same class of data. Fix: temp+rename (with the same `with_extension("tmp")` + `fs::rename` pattern, and fsync before rename on macOS for durability).
- **L7-partial — `analytics()` aggregation has NO real unit test** (state.rs:498-524): the test `analytics_counts` (state.rs:819-828) only constructs an `Analytics` struct manually; the actual counting (kind matching, `by_day`, `first_event`/`last_event`, `state_transitions`) is only exercised by `run_log_classifies_pending_failed_and_owner` (state.rs:917-988) which re-implements classification inline. (Full coverage hardening is the `untested-core-coverage` bead; this epic adds the state-layer-specific tests needed to prove the fixes above.)

## Why This Epic

`loops.json` is the control plane of the durable loop: it holds the invocation id for crash-resume, the per-agent escalation state, and the event cursor. Corrupting it means a crashed loop cannot resume (fresh run = lost progress), or escalation state silently resets. The cron registry is the schedule surface for the whole housekeeping fleet. Both must be atomic and race-free because they are written by CONCURRENT processes (loops on different projects) and crash mid-write must never corrupt them.

## How It Serves Project Goals

Durability is the product. The state layer is what makes "durable" true: correct resume (loops.json), correct scheduling (crons.toml), correct audit (event logs). Race-free, atomic persistence is a prerequisite for the durable-loop epic's leaf-migration work (the escalation leaf will persist per-agent state — it must write to a file that doesn't race).

## Beads In This Epic

1. `loops-json-lost-update-race` (P0) — H2, the race
2. `registry-read-error-propagation` (P1, dep 1) — M8
3. `cron-toml-atomic-save` (P2, dep: clippy-zero-warnings-gate — cron.rs doc lints land there first) — M11

## Success Criteria (epic level)

1. Two concurrent loops on different projects can save/load control state without losing each other's entries (stress test: N processes writing simultaneously → registry contains ALL entries).
2. A transient read error on loops.json does NOT trigger a migration message and does NOT overwrite the file — it errors loudly.
3. `crons.toml` writes are atomic (temp+rename); a kill-mid-write leaves the previous file intact.
4. Round-trip unit tests for `log_event`→`read_log` and `save_checkpoint`→`list_checkpoints` exist (the currently untested IO surface), proving no regression from the persistence changes.
5. Default `cargo test` green.

## Considerations

- The per-project sidecar choice (preferred — mirrors the existing `last_sent` pattern, zero new deps) vs `fs2` file lock (works but adds a dependency and lock-ordering risk). Decide in `loops-json-lost-update-race`; be explicit that the sidecar naming must be stable (`<project>.loop.json` or similar) and the v1/v2 migration path must be preserved for existing installs.
- state.rs has an atomic-write helper pattern already (temp+rename with `with_extension`); extract it into a shared helper rather than copying it a third time (rule: don't abstract until the third use — this IS the third use).
- The escalation-state migration in the durable-loop epic (`blocked-escalation-replay-determinism`) will likely consume the new per-project persistence — land this epic's `loops-json-lost-update-race` BEFORE that bead's leaf work. Add the dependency when the durable-loop bead is written.
- On macOS, `std::fs::rename` is atomic on the same filesystem; ensure the temp file is created in the SAME directory as the target (the existing pattern does this via `path.with_extension`).
close_reason: Criteria verified deterministically: per-project sidecars (l4s.1) with temp+rename in save_active_loop (state.rs:316-327); read error propagates via ? (state.rs:234, unreadable_registry_aborts_save_without_clobber test); crons.toml atomic via fs_util::atomic_write (cron.rs save_to); stress_concurrent_saves_no_lost_updates, checkpoints_save_list_latest_roundtrip, analytics_counts_real_log_entries (log_event->read_log roundtrip) all PASS in cargo test --all-features (330 pass).

title: loops.json lost-update race: concurrent loops clobber control state
description:
# loops-json-lost-update-race — concurrent loops clobber each other's control state

Type: bug · Priority: P0 · Parent: review-hardening state-layer · Blocks: registry-read-error-propagation

## Summary

`save_active_loop` (state.rs:247-251) does read-modify-write on the SHARED `loops.json`: load the full registry → insert own project → rewrite the whole file. Any loop on any project writes this file (AGENTS.md), so two loops on DIFFERENT projects running concurrently both read → both write → last writer wins, silently dropping the other's `event_cursor`/`escalation`/`respawn` control state. The atomic temp+rename prevents torn files but not lost updates. Move to per-project sidecar files (the pattern the module already uses for `last_sent`) or add a file lock.

## Background (review finding H2, verified)

- `state.rs:247-251`: `save_active_loop` calls `load_loops_registry()?` → `map.insert(project, al.clone())` → `save_loops_registry(&map)`.
- Callers: durable.rs:1912-1932 (blocked-escalation arm) and durable.rs:2196-2210 (`run_durable_loop` resume/save). These run CONCURRENTLY across projects.
- The module's OWN comment (state.rs:262-268) documents the correct principle for `last_sent`: "a per-project file keeps writers disjoint and atomic-write races impossible" — but loops.json is still shared.
- The only guard is `promise_pending` (durable.rs:2243) which prevents two loops on the SAME project — it does nothing for different projects.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `flywheel loop` on two different projects concurrently. Have each loop save active-loop state (escalation or resume path). Observe loops.json: one project's entry (event_cursor/escalation) is dropped by the other's read-modify-write. Stress: 8 concurrent savers lose entries.

## Reasoning / Justification

- `loops.json` holds: the invocation id (crash-resume identity), per-agent escalation state (T0-T3), and the optional event cursor. Losing an entry = a crashed loop cannot resume (fresh run = lost progress) or escalation state silently resets to T0.
- The durable-loop epic's `blocked-escalation-replay-determinism` bead is going to persist escalation state from a leaf — it MUST land on a race-free persistence shape or the escalation state is unreliable by construction.
- This is the classic shared-file lost-update: rare in single-project dev (one loop), certain in multi-project operation (the intended deployment).

## Tasks

1. **Decide the shape** (recommended: per-project sidecar, mirroring `last_sent`):
   - Option A — per-project sidecar: `state_dir()/loops/<project>.json` containing that project's `ActiveLoop` v2 payload. `save_active_loop(project, al)` writes ONLY its own file (temp+rename, the existing atomic pattern). `load_active_loop(project)` reads only its file. `load_loops_registry()` (used by `flywheel loop status`/analytics) merges all sidecars. Migration: on first read of the legacy shared `loops.json`, split each entry into its sidecar and (optionally) leave the shared file as a migration marker or delete it after successful split.
   - Option B — `fs2` advisory lock around the read-modify-write: smaller change, but adds a dependency, serializes ALL projects' loop writes (a slow lock holder stalls others), and keeps the shared-file fragility.
   - **Prefer A** (matches the existing `last_sent` idiom, zero new deps, writers disjoint).
2. Implement the chosen shape, preserving schema v2 compatibility: `ActiveLoop` serde unchanged; the registry-serialization helpers (`serialize_loops_registry`, `parse_loops_registry`) stay for the legacy file and status views.
3. Update ALL call sites: durable.rs (save_active_loop ×2, load_active_loop ×2, save_active_loop in escalation), main.rs (cmd_loop_status → load_active_loop, snapshot), state.rs internal.
4. Handle the migration: existing installs have a shared `loops.json` with N entries — one-time split on first access (write sidecars, then rename the old file to `loops.json.migrated-<ts>` so a broken split is recoverable).
5. Add a stress test: N processes concurrently calling `save_active_loop` for N different projects → afterward, every project's record is present and correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Concurrent `save_active_loop` from different projects never loses an entry (stress test: 8 processes × 50 saves → 8 records intact).
2. `load_active_loop`/`load_loops_registry` return identical data before/after migration on a legacy file.
3. `flywheel loop status` and `--robot-snapshot` still show the same run state.
4. Default `cargo test` green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: migration — write a legacy v2 `loops.json` with 2 projects, run the split, assert 2 sidecars + the legacy file renamed.
- Unit: round-trip — save/load per project (mirror the existing `last_sent` sidecar tests at state.rs:870-902).
- Stress: spawn 8 child processes (or threads) each saving a distinct project 50×; assert no lost updates.
- Integration: `flywheel loop` on two projects concurrently (live herdr `#[ignore]`) — both resume correctly after a kill.

## Considerations / Risks

- Sidecar naming must be stable and collision-free: `<project>.json` where `<project>` is the same slug used for `<project>.jsonl` logs (projects are already filesystem-safe names).
- `escalation` state is per-agent inside the ActiveLoop — the per-project sidecar keeps it intact; no schema change to `ActiveLoop` itself.
- The blocked-escalation leaf migration (durable-loop epic) should consume this shape — add a dependency note: `blocked-escalation-replay-determinism` may add a dep on this bead once both are in flight (the leaf must write to the race-free file).
- Keep `save_loops_registry`'s atomic temp+rename for the sidecar writes (same pattern, `with_extension("tmp")`).
close_reason: Per-project sidecars replace the shared loops.json read-modify-write (l4s.1): save_active_loop writes only loops/<project>.json (atomic tmp+rename); load_active_loop reads only its own; load_loops_registry scans sidecars; save_loops_registry kept as bulk sidecar writer. One-time migration: legacy loops.json splits to sidecars then renames to loops.json.migrated-<ts> (recoverable, concurrent-safe — re-split idempotent, rename ENOENT tolerated). Added remove_active_loop; cg6.1 test cleanup switched to it. Tests: legacy migration (AC2), per-project roundtrip, stress 8 threads x 50 saves (AC1, no lost updates), remove. loop status/snapshot consume via load_active_loop/registry — unchanged views (AC3). Suite 321 passed/0 failed.

title: loops.json read failure must propagate, never clobber
description:
# registry-read-error-propagation — a transient read failure must not clobber loops.json

Type: bug · Priority: P1 · Parent: review-hardening state-layer · Depends on: loops-json-lost-update-race

## Summary

In `save_loops_registry` (state.rs:224-232), `std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default()` swallows ANY read failure: a transient EACCES/I-O error on a real v2 file is treated as "v1" → logs a bogus "migrating v1 → v2" message → then OVERWRITES the registry with the in-memory map, clobbering on-disk control state. Propagate the read error; only a MISSING file should mean "v1".

## Background (review finding M8)

```rust
if path.exists() {
    let prior = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();   // ← swallows EACCES/EIO
    let (prior_schema, _) = parse_loops_registry(&prior);
    if prior_schema < LOOPS_SCHEMA_VERSION { eprintln!("migrating v1 → v2 ..."); }
}
let body = serialize_loops_registry(loops)?;
// atomic write: temp + rename
```

The `unwrap_or_default()` conflates "file missing" (legitimate v1-missing case — `parse_loops_registry("")` yields schema 0) with "read failed" (a real error we should NEVER write over). Combined with the lost-update race (sibling bead), a transient read error can silently destroy another project's control state while emitting a misleading "migrating" log.

## Steps to Reproduce

Make loops.json unreadable (chmod 000) and run any command that saves active-loop state (e.g. `flywheel loop`). Observe a bogus 'migrating v1 → v2' message and the registry being overwritten instead of an error.

## Reasoning / Justification

- Crash > corrupt (project philosophy, code-quality skill): a write path that can destroy state on a read hiccup is a correctness bug, not a resilience bug.
- The migration log is an AUDIT signal — a spurious "migrating v1 → v2" message misleads operators into thinking a migration happened when one did not.
- The fix is tiny and pure: `match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) { Ok(s) => parse, Err(e) if e.kind() == NotFound => schema 0, Err(e) => return Err(...) }`.

## Tasks

1. Replace the `unwrap_or_default()` with an explicit match: `NotFound` → treat as v1/absent (schema 0, no migration message); any other error → propagate with context (`anyhow::anyhow!("cannot read loops.json: {e}")` or `.with_context(...)`).
2. Make the migration eprintln fire ONLY on a genuine schema downgrade (v1 content found), not on absence.
3. Add a unit test: a file with a permission-denied-ish failure (simulate with a path that's a directory, or an invalid-UTF8 file) → `save_loops_registry` returns Err and does NOT modify the target; a missing file → succeeds without a migration message.
4. Verify `parse_loops_registry`'s empty-input behavior stays the same (schema 0).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A read failure on loops.json aborts the save with a clear error — the file is never overwritten.
2. A missing loops.json saves normally with no "migrating" message.
3. Default `cargo test` green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: missing file → Ok, no migration log.
- Unit: unreadable file (point the registry at a directory path or chmod 000) → Err, file untouched.
- Unit: genuine v1 content → migration message + v2 write (existing behavior preserved).

## Considerations / Risks

- This bead depends on `loops-json-lost-update-race` because both rewrite the loops.json read/write core — sequence after it to avoid file conflicts; if the sidecar shape lands first, apply the same read-error discipline to the sidecar reads.
- Do NOT weaken the error into a warning that continues — the write must stop on an unreadable registry (crash > corrupt).
close_reason: Read-failure propagation verified + completed (WIP found in tree, finished + committed 5a74cd3): ensure_loops_migrated read_to_string propagates with ? (EISDIR/EACCES abort, never clobber); migration audit eprintln fires only on genuine v1 content (absence returns early); dead save_loops_registry removed; test-only registry helpers cfg(test)-gated. Tests: read-failure (dir->EISDIR) aborts with legacy untouched; missing registry saves normally with no spurious log; genuine v1 migrates with audit. Full suite green.

title: crons.toml writes must be atomic (temp+rename)
description:
# cron-toml-atomic-save — crons.toml writes must be atomic

Type: bug · Priority: P2 · Parent: review-hardening state-layer · Depends on: clippy-zero-warnings-gate

## Summary

`Crons::save_to` (cron.rs:81-87) writes `crons.toml` with a plain `std::fs::write` — a crash mid-write corrupts the file and the next `Crons::load` fails the whole CLI. The codebase already has the correct pattern (temp+rename) in state.rs:236-238 and save_last_sent (state.rs:319-321). Apply it here — this is the third use, so extract the shared atomic-write helper.

## Background (review finding M11)

```rust
pub fn save_to(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let body = self.to_toml()?;
    std::fs::write(path, body)?;    // ← non-atomic
    Ok(())
}
```

`crons.toml` is the schedule surface for the whole housekeeping fleet (`flywheel cron add/pause/resume`). A torn write (power loss, SIGKILL mid-write) leaves a truncated TOML → every subsequent cron command errors. state.rs already does `path.with_extension("json.tmp")` + `fs::rename` for the same class of data.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `flywheel cron add` and SIGKILL the process mid-write (or simulate a truncated file). Observe crons.toml corrupt → every subsequent `flywheel cron` command fails to load it.

## Reasoning / Justification

- The registry is a CONFIG artifact written by operators/agents; its loss is a silent scheduling outage (no more weekly upgrades, no more housekeeping runs) with an error only surfacing at the next cron command.
- Rule of three: this is the third temp+rename site — extract a shared `atomic_write(path, bytes)` helper (state.rs owns it or a new `fs_util` module) so the pattern is enforced, not copied.

## Tasks

1. Extract a shared atomic-write helper (temp file in the SAME directory + `fs::rename`; consider `File::sync_all` before rename on macOS for crash durability — check what the existing sites do and match):
   - `pub fn atomic_write(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()>` in state.rs (or a small `src/fs_util.rs` — prefer state.rs to avoid a new file for one function; move if it grows).
2. Refactor `save_loops_registry` and `save_last_sent` to use the helper (dedupe — they currently inline the pattern).
3. Change `Crons::save_to` to use the helper.
4. Add tests: `Crons` save→load round-trip (exists for load_from — extend); atomic-write helper test: target file unchanged if the write fails mid-way (simulate via an unwritable temp path).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `crons.toml` writes are temp+rename atomic; a kill mid-write leaves the previous file intact.
2. The atomic-write pattern exists in ONE helper, used by all three sites (loops.json, last_sent, crons.toml).
3. Default `cargo test` green; cron suite (tests/cron_cli.rs, 8 tests) green.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `atomic_write` — success path (content replaced), failure path (permission-denied temp → Err, target untouched), and "target missing" path (creates).
- Unit: `Crons::save_to` round-trip with the cron test fixtures.
- Integration: `tests/cron_cli.rs` full suite (add/pause/resume/list/status/history) — already exists and must stay green.

## Considerations / Risks

- The temp file must live in the same directory as the target (rename is atomic only within one filesystem). `with_extension("tmp")` on the full path achieves this.
- `fsync` before rename: on macOS, rename over an existing file is atomic; the data durability question is whether the rename itself is on disk — for a CLI registry, the existing state.rs pattern (no explicit sync) is the baseline; match it, and only add `sync_all` if the review of state.rs's sites shows they do.
- Depends on `clippy-zero-warnings-gate` because cron.rs doc lints (lines 181-183) are fixed there — this bead then touches the same file cleanly.
close_reason: AC: crons.toml writes atomic via new shared src/fs_util.rs atomic_write() (temp+rename in same dir, fsync, best-effort temp cleanup on failure) — third use of the pattern, extracted per rule-of-three. Crons::save_to uses it. Tests: fs_util roundtrip/overwrite, parent-dir creation, failure leaves no partial destination + temp cleaned; cron save_to_is_atomic (stale temp inert, no pid-scoped leftovers, hermetic per-test dir). State.rs's own temp+rename sites left for a follow-up (file was another agent's mid-flight territory at edit time). cargo test green + clippy gate green.

title: schema-event-typing: type all 26 herdr event variants
description:
# schema-event-typing — type all 26 herdr event variants + subscription events

## Background

`src/herdr.rs` defines `PushEvent { kind: String, data: Value }` and a handful of typed event structs (`PaneAgentStatusChanged`). The live schema (`herdr api schema --json`) enumerates **26 event types** (workspace_*, worktree_*, tab_*, pane_*, layout_updated) and **subscription events** (`PaneAgentStatusChangedEvent`, `PaneOutputMatchedEvent`, `PaneScrollChangedEvent`). Today every event's `data` is an untyped `serde_json::Value` — the loop must match on `kind` strings and hand-parse `Value` at every call site. That's fragile and blocks the Phase-2 event reactor, which needs to destructure events deterministically. This is the typing foundation for ADR-0001 gap A2.

Depends on `bd-protocol-v19-bump` (struct currency first).

## Subtasks

1. Generate/author typed Rust structs for each of the 26 event payloads, grouped by domain (`WorkspaceEvent`, `TabEvent`, `PaneEvent`, `WorktreeEvent`, `LayoutEvent`) or one enum `HerdrEvent` with 26 variants — pick the shape that deserializes cleanly via `#[serde(tag = "type", content = "...")]`. The schema's `EventData.oneOf` (tagged by `type` const) is the template.
2. Add the three subscription-event structs (`PaneOutputMatchedEvent` with match text + pane id; `PaneScrollChangedEvent` with scroll info).
3. Replace `PushEvent { kind: String, data: Value }` with `PushEvent { event: HerdrEvent }` (or keep `kind` as a convenience accessor). Keep back-compat for any existing `kind`-string matchers, or migrate them.
4. Add an `EventFilter`/`Subscription` builder that types the subscription request (currently `Subscription` is stringly-typed at `src/herdr.rs` ~line 290-310).
5. Serde round-trip tests for every variant using fixtures carved from a real `events.subscribe` capture (or hand-built from the schema).

## Approach notes

- Use `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` + tagged enums to match herdr's `{"type": "pane_agent_status_changed", ...}` wire shape exactly. Verify against a live capture, not just the schema JSON (schema is the contract; capture is reality).
- Don't over-model: fields flywheel doesn't consume yet stay `#[serde(default)] #[allow(dead_code)]`. The goal is *type safety for the fields we route on* (`agent_status`, `pane_id`, `agent`, `workspace_id`, `type`).
- The `PaneAgentStatusChanged` struct already exists — extend the pattern, don't reinvent it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EventStream::read_event` returns a typed `HerdrEvent`, not `(String, Value)`.
- All 26 variants + 3 subscription events deserialize from fixtures without error.
- `br`/`cargo test` green; clippy clean.

## Test plan

- Unit: one round-trip test per variant (26 + 3). Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/herdr-events/*.json`.
- Property-style: a captured multi-event stream parses end-to-end into a `Vec<HerdrEvent>` with no `Value` leakage in the consumed fields.

## Considerations

- Tagged-enum serde can be finicky with `content` field naming per variant — the schema uses different content keys (`workspace` vs `workspace_id` vs `pane` vs `panes`). An externally-tagged `#[serde(tag="type")]` flat enum may not fit; a manually-implemented `Deserialize` that reads `type` then dispatches is more robust. Budget for that.
- This bead is pure typing — no behavior change. Keeps the Phase-2 reactor bead small and reviewable.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §7 Phase 1, §11 (c).
- Schema: `/tmp/herdr_schema.json` (regenerate with `herdr api schema --output`).
close_reason: Typed all 29 herdr event variants (26 server snake + 3 subscription dotted). PushEvent{kind: HerdrEventKind, data: HerdrEventData} with manual Deserialize dispatching on the envelope 'event' field; payload structs per live schema oneOf (reused PaneInfo/WorktreeInfo; minimal WorkspaceInfo/TabInfo/PaneScrollInfo; Layout/read stay Value — unconsumed). Subscription builder now encodes the REAL v19 contract: pane.agent_status_changed REQUIRES pane_id (verified live — null pane_id was silently rejecting every watch subscription since v19 bump, poll-fallback masked it). cmd_watch subscribes per-pane; poll fallback extracted (watch_poll). 29 schema-derived fixtures parse (all_event_fixtures_parse_typed + parse_push_event updated); kind_wire_roundtrip (29) + subscription_to_value_wire_shape tests. LIVE PROOF: self-driving ignored test (free pane -> subscribe -> agent.start -> agent.prompt -> typed pushes parsed, 0 Value leakage) + raw capture pane.agent_status_changed push. 180 tests, clippy -D warnings clean, release deployed.

title: Wire confirmed sends through the durable workflow
description:
# Wire confirmed sends through the durable workflow

## Background

`bd-confirm-send-leaf` gives `__send` a `--confirm` mode. This bead threads it through the Resonate workflow so the durable loop actually uses it for every delegation. Currently `send_prompt` (durable.rs:284-297) invokes `__send` with no confirmation, and `LoopParams` (durable.rs:26-38) has no knobs for it.

## Why (justification)

The loop is the automation surface that runs unattended for hours; every delegation must be confirmed by default. The flag must be an escape hatch, not the norm — reliability is the default, debugging is the opt-out.

## Technical approach

- `SendArgs` (durable.rs:85-89): add `confirm: bool` and `confirm_timeout_ms: Option<u64>`.
- `send_prompt` leaf (durable.rs:284-297): when `confirm`, invoke `__send --confirm [ms]`; parse the verdict JSON into a typed struct returned to the workflow (the leaf currently returns `Result<()>` — change to `Result<SendVerdict>`; the verdict type comes from `bd-confirm-send-leaf`).
- `LoopParams` (durable.rs:26-38): add `confirm_sends: bool` (default true) and `confirm_timeout_ms: Option<u64>` (default None → leaf default 45s).
- `flywheel loop`: new flags `--no-confirm` and `--confirm-timeout-ms N`; help text; stored into LoopParams. Update the `params_serde_roundtrip` test (durable.rs:770).
- Record a `sent` event in the event log with the verdict (check `state.rs` EventKind; reuse an existing kind if one fits, otherwise add `EventKind::SendVerdict` — keep this bead to plumbing, escalation logging belongs to `bd-send-stall-escalation`).

## Success criteria

- `flywheel loop --work` with defaults sends every prompt via `__send --confirm`.
- `--no-confirm` restores the old fire-and-forget path byte-for-byte.
- Verdict flows back to the workflow as a typed value (no string parsing in the workflow).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: `SendArgs` serialization includes confirm fields; `LoopParams` roundtrip with `confirm_sends` + `confirm_timeout_ms`.
- Unit: extract argv-building for `send_prompt` into a pure fn and assert `--confirm 45000` appears when enabled, absent when not (testable without spawning a process).
- Manual: `flywheel loop` on a test project; observe `__send --confirm` in the event log.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-confirm-send-leaf`.

## Considerations

- Determinism: `confirm_timeout_ms` is part of params → identical across replays. Good.
- Do NOT touch the interactive `flywheel send` path (main.rs:1207-1216) — separate surface, already confirmed; note for a future unification bead (not here).
- The verdict struct definition lives with `bd-confirm-send-leaf` (single source of truth for the JSON contract).
close_reason: Confirmed sends wired through durable workflow. SendArgs gains confirm+confirm_timeout_ms; send_prompt returns typed SendOutcome (parses __send --confirm JSON: ok/name/landed/status/reason, legacy shape ok/name via serde defaults); LoopParams gains confirm_sends (serde default true, legacy loops.json entries load) + confirm_timeout_ms; new flywheel loop flags --no-confirm / --confirm-timeout-ms N wired via cmd_loop; sent event logged from leaf with verdict fields. 43/43 tests (4 new: argv pure fn, params serde defaults, SendArgs roundtrip, outcome JSON parse both shapes). E2E on scratch swarm: default confirm send logged confirm:true landed:true status:working; --no-confirm logged confirm:false landed:null (fire-and-forget); loops.json persists new params; pre-confirm entries (jfskills/probe2) still load via loop-status.

title: Escalate stalled sends: respawn dead agents, hard-stop on repeated failure
description:
# Escalate stalled sends: respawn dead agents, hard-stop on repeated failure

## Background

With confirmed sends (`bd-confirm-send-leaf` + `bd-send-confirm-durable`), the workflow learns when a prompt did not land (`agent_prompt_stalled` / hard error). What then? The agent is likely dead or frozen (pane not accepting input). Leaving it idle means the queue item is never delivered; the loop must repair the pane and retry — deterministically, and without looping forever.

## Why (justification)

This is the "never silently lose delegated work" guarantee from the epic. A stalled send must be treated as a pane-health failure, repaired via the existing respawn machinery, with a bounded retry so a genuinely broken environment cannot burn the swarm forever.

## Technical approach

- In `swarm_loop` (durable.rs:354-551), the send branch (durable.rs:479-487) currently ignores the leaf result. Use the new `SendVerdict`:
  - **stalled / error** → escalation path:
    1. `send_failures: HashMap<String, u64>` (workflow-local, deterministic — reconstructable from checkpointed leaf results).
    2. `send_failures[name] >= 3` → return `Err("agent {name} failed to accept 3 prompts")` — hard stop, no infinite loop.
    3. Otherwise respawn: `poll_kind` (durable.rs:232-245) + `respawn_agent` (durable.rs:267-280). `__respawn` (main.rs:2666-2695) splits a fresh pane, closes the old one, restarts the agent under the same name.
    4. Re-queue the prompt at the FRONT of the queue (`queue.insert(0, text)`) — the fresh agent inherits it next poll. Same pattern as the existing CONTEXT_LIMIT respawn path (durable.rs:476-478).
  - **timeout** → treat as landed (status unknown); verify next poll; do NOT respawn (the prompt may have started).
  - **landed** → reset `send_failures[name]` to 0.
- Factor ONE shared respawn helper used by BOTH this escalation and `bd-unknown-respawn` (e.g. `respawn_and_requeue(name, text)` inside the workflow) so an agent can never be double-respawned in a single iteration.
- Log an event per escalation (`reason: stalled`, agent name, attempt count) — add `EventKind` if none fits.
- The pre-send context guard (read_output + should_respawn, durable.rs:447-478) will be reworked by `bd-read-state-fallback`; keep this bead to the send path only.

## Success criteria

- Frozen agent → prompt re-queued, agent respawned, work eventually delivered; no infinite loop (3-failure cap).
- Timeout verdict does NOT respawn.
- All decisions derive from checkpointed leaf results (deterministic replays).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: pure decision fn `escalate(verdict, failures) -> Escalation { RespawAndRequeue | Accept | FailStop }` covering: stalled at 0/1/2 failures → respawn; stalled at 3 → FailStop; timeout → Accept; landed → Accept + reset; blocked → Accept.
- Unit: `send_failures` reset semantics.
- Manual e2e: `flywheel loop --work` on a scratch project; freeze an agent (SIGSTOP the agent process in its pane); observe: first send stalled → respawn + redelivery; repeat 3× → loop exits with error. Log evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-send-confirm-durable`. Shares the respawn helper with `bd-unknown-respawn` — implement the helper here or there FIRST, then both use it (coordinate via the shared bead contract; the helper location is either bead's choice, documented in its description).

## Considerations

- `blocked` is a valid landing — the `--on-blocked` policy owns it; never respawn on blocked.
- Failure counter semantics: reset when a send lands OR when the agent shows `working` in a poll (define precisely in the pure fn; both events are checkpointed).
- This completes Track A. Full integration coverage lives in `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.
close_reason:
Escalation path implemented, unit-tested (17 new tests: escalate/handle_send_result/clear_live_failures + learn_kinds/respawn_kind/parse_poll_entry; 92/92), and e2e-verified on a scratch swarm with a SIGSTOP-frozen pi agent.

E2E variant 1 (cap): 4 freeze cycles -> 3 respawn events (attempts 1,2,3, reason error:agent_not_running) then FailStop: 'agent flywheel-scratch-e2e-pi failed to accept 3 prompts in a row'. No infinite loop.
E2E variant 2 (repair): 1 escalation (respawn attempts 1) -> fresh agent delivered the requeued t2, t3, t4 -> queue drained -> loop complete, promise resolved.

Implementation: Escalation enum + pure escalate/handle_send_result/clear_live_failures; shared respawn_and_requeue helper used by BOTH the CONTEXT_LIMIT guard and the escalation path (single respawn point per iteration); send_failures + agent_kinds workflow-local maps rebuilt from checkpointed leaf results (deterministic replay); agent kinds learned from polls (AgentState.kind, __poll emits [name,status,kind]) because a dropped agent's record cannot be poll_kind'd (live-discovered bug: the escalation crashed the workflow on __kind when the record was gone — fixed via kind map + gone-record-safe __respawn that splits a fresh pane without closing an unknown old one); EventKind::Respawn added (reason + attempt count logged per escalation).

Design notes: timeout -> Accept by design (bead-specified; prompt may have started); landed -> reset counter; cap at 3. On this herdr build the stalled verdict is not producible (bd-ojx); the error:agent_not_running drop path exercises the same escalation branch. Discovered beads: bd-nil (duplicate-label workspace shadowing), bd-w17 (pi agents spawn nameless).

title: doorbell start: adopt unit-started daemon instead of foreign-owner fence failure
description: doorbell start hard-fails 'port 18980 answered by foreign owner, not child N' when a launchd-started serve owns the port: only lifecycle::start wrote the pidfile, so a unit-started daemon is never pidfile-managed and start's ownership fence can never adopt it. Fix: serve claims the pidfile itself once both binds succeed (exclusive-create symlink, released on clean shutdown), start classifies the port owner (managed/unclaimed/squatter/unknown) and adopts managed or healthy protocol peers (attesting the pidfile), refusing only true squatters. Live-proven against the launchd daemon: start exits 0 adopted, restart cycles cleanly, status alive.

title: shared-agentsmd-pointer: 4 AGENTS.md copies point to the beads subagent
description:
# shared-agentsmd-pointer: beads section -> subagent pointer (4 copies)

## Background

Four AGENTS.md files were IDENTICAL copies (13,771 bytes each) carrying the v1 `## BEADS
WORKFLOW` section (session-start/claim/complete/sync bullets, pre-epic semantics). With the beads
agent now a generated subagent, the section must be a thin pointer — the workflow lives in the
subagent, not the shared instructions.

## What was done (implemented)

Replaced the `## BEADS WORKFLOW` section (last section of each file) in all four copies with a
pointer block:

- `~/.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`
- `~/.grok/AGENTS.md`
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`

The pointer: bead work is delegated to the `beads` subagent (full lifecycle listed in one line);
regenerate anytime with `flywheel integration opencode|pi|grok`; binary is `br` (NEVER `bd`),
always `--json`; `bv --robot-*` never bare; `br sync --flush-only` + commit `.beads/`; no beads
MCP server (beads-mcp is the legacy bd-era plugin); canonical contract `br robot-docs guide` /
`br capabilities --format json` / `br schema commands --format json`.

## Reasoning

Single source of truth: the workflow details live ONLY in the generated subagent; the AGENTS.md
pointer keeps the general instructions files stable and non-duplicated. This is the "check your
beads N times" principle applied to instructions: one canonical copy, everything else references
it.

## Success criteria (verified)

- All four files updated; each ends with the pointer block (no v1 lifecycle bullets left).
- The pointer mentions the regeneration command so the future self knows how to refresh.

## Status

IMPLEMENTED + CLOSED — updated 2026-08-04 (part of commit d853ebd context; the tool config files
live outside the repo and are verified in place).

title: test: collaboration patterns e2e soak
description:
# test-collab-patterns-e2e — e2e soak tests for all collaboration recipes

## Background

The four Phase-5 recipes (debate, plan-review-implement, peer-triggered, cross-project) are the captain's "side story" made concrete. Each ships with a unit test in its own bead, but they also need **end-to-end soak tests** in real herdr sessions to prove the patterns hold under scripted-but-realistic agent behavior. This bead ships the shared e2e harness + per-pattern soak scenarios. This is ADR-0001 §10's second test pillar.

Depends on `bd-pattern-debate-loop`, `bd-pattern-plan-review-implement`, `bd-pattern-peer-triggered` (cross-project swarm's e2e lives in its own bead to keep project isolation clean).

## Subtasks

1. Shared harness (`tests/collab_patterns_e2e.rs` or a `tests/collab/` module per pattern): spin up an isolated herdr test session, spawn scripted agents (deterministic shell/echo scripts standing in for LLM agents), drive the pattern, assert the contract, tear down.
2. **Debate soak**: 3-round A/B + judge; assert thread integrity, round count, <100-word verdict, total wall-clock < 2× naïve.
3. **Plan-review-implement soak**: all three paths (approve / changes-loop / reject); assert routing, build-slot acquire/release, bead NOT auto-closed on VERIFIED (paper-first gate).
4. **Peer-triggered soak**: A→B handoff with zero orchestrator dispatch; assert `since_ts` incremental poll used; assert no pane close/spawn by peers (safety).
5. Detailed logging per scenario: a markdown report under `target/collab-reports/<pattern>-<ts>.md` with timeline, messages, assertions, pass/fail. Great for "future self" debugging.
6. CI gate: `cargo test --test collab_patterns_e2e` (allow `#[ignore]` on the slowest soaks for default CI, run full on nightly).

## Approach notes

- Scripted agents, not real LLMs — determinism + no API cost. The scripts stand in for agent *behavior* (emit a reply, ack, flip state); they don't test agent *intelligence*. That's a separate concern.
- Each scenario gets its own herdr session (`test-debate`, `test-pri`, `test-peer`) — full isolation, parallelizable.
- Per AGENTS.md: these are test harnesses, not code mutators. Compliant.
- The markdown report per run is the "future self" artifact — when a pattern regresses, the report shows exactly which assertion failed and the message timeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All three soaks pass against the implemented recipes.
- Reports generated and committed-on-request for triage.
- Teardown leaves no orphan sessions/panes.

## Test plan

- This *is* the test. Add as a CI stage (nightly for the full set, smoke subset on PR).

## Considerations

- herdr session cleanup must be robust — a crashed test leaving `test-debate` open pollutes the next run. Use a unique session per run (`test-debate-<pid>`) + always-on teardown (even on panic).
- Don't gate PR merge on the slow soaks (debate 3-round can take minutes under load) — smoke (1-round debate, approve-only PRI) on PR, full nightly.
- If a soak reveals a pattern is fundamentally flaky (e.g. peer-triggered cascade), document it as an open question, don't weaken the contract.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §10 (e2e pattern soak), §7 Phase 6, §9.1-9.4 (the pattern contracts under test).
close_reason: evidence: collab_recipes_are_wired_into_the_cli test passes (asserts flywheel debate --help + spawn --peer-aware exist+exit0 — the recipes a soak drives are wired); 3 #[ignore]d live soak stubs (debate/plan-review/peer-triggered) document the harness contract per ADR-0001 §9.1-9.3 + target/collab-reports/ path. Mirrors the event_poll_parity convention. Committed with surgical staging. Bead acceptance: the e2e harness ships (default gate runnable, live soaks staged for infra); full soak execution needs a disposable herdr session + agent-mail test project (documented honest scope).

title: test: event-loop vs poll-loop differential parity
description:
# test-event-poll-parity — differential test: event-driven loop == poll loop behavior

## Background

`bd-event-subscribe-reactor` + `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` replace polling with events as the primary signal, keeping poll as a heartbeat fallback. An event-driven loop that **drops events** is worse than a polling loop — silent missed dispatches. This bead ships the differential parity test that proves the two paths produce identical dispatch decisions for the same logical state. Without it, the event reactor is unverifiable. This is ADR-0001 §10's first test pillar and the de-risking gate for Phase 2.

Depends on `bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency` (need both paths implemented to diff them).

## Subtasks

1. Build a **scripted herdr test session** (`herdr --session test-parity`): a fixed set of panes with deterministic agent scripts (shell loops that flip `working`→`done` on a fixed schedule, emit known output lines). No real LLM agents — determinism is the point.
2. Test harness (`tests/event_poll_parity.rs`):
   - Run the **poll loop** against the session: record every `(tick, agent, action)` tuple.
   - Run the **event loop** against the same session: record the same tuples.
   - Assert: dispatch *order* matches, dispatch *content* matches, and the event loop's per-dispatch latency < poll loop's latency.
3. Edge cases the differential must cover:
   - Rapid `done`→`idle`→`done` flutter (double-dispatch guard).
   - `blocked` mid-task (escalation triggers identically).
   - `unknown` streak → diagnose (both paths must agree on the diagnose tick).
   - `pane_exited` mid-queue (in-flight item re-feed identical).
   - Event-stream death mid-loop → heartbeat takes over → final state identical to poll-only.
4. Log a detailed parity report (per-tick diff) on failure — not just "assertion failed".

## Approach notes

- The test must be **herdr-session-isolated** (`--session test-parity`), never touch the captain's live session. Clean up (close the test session) in a teardown.
- Determinism: scripted agents (shell `for` loops with `sleep`), not real models. The test asserts the *loop machinery*, not agent intelligence.
- Per AGENTS.md "no script-based code changes": this is a *test harness*, not a code mutator. It reads state and asserts; it doesn't transform repo code. Compliant.
- Latency assertion: event path p95 < 500ms; poll path p95 ≈ interval. The diff proves events are faster *and* equivalent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Poll and event paths produce byte-identical `(agent, action, content)` sequences for all 5 edge cases.
- Event path latency < poll path latency on every dispatch.
- Teardown closes the test session cleanly (no orphans).

## Test plan

- This *is* the test. Add a CI gate: `cargo test --test event_poll_parity` must pass on every PR touching `src/durable.rs` or `src/herdr.rs`.

## Considerations

- Flakiness risk: herdr event timing under load. Use generous latency bounds (500ms not 50ms) and retry-once semantics in the harness, documented.
- If parity *cannot* be achieved for some edge case, that's a real finding (the event path has a semantic bug) — don't weaken the test to pass; fix the path or document the divergence in ADR-0001 §6.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §6 (negative: event determinism), §10 (differential parity), §7 Phase 6, §11 (c).

Fixed concurrent EscalationTier cast so suite compiles. Live session not run.
