title: toron-superlogical-stubs: Unsupported stubs reserve env names
description:
# toron-superlogical-stubs — reserve env names + `Unsupported` stubs for unreleased/future backends

## Background

`FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical|tmux` and `FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron` are documented future selections (ADR-0002 §3.1). superlogical is unreleased; toron-core isn't shipped as an embeddable crate yet; tmux is on hold (toron ADR-0003). If a user sets these env values today, they must get a **clear, actionable error**, not a silent fallback to herdr/agentmail (which would hide misconfiguration) nor a compile error (which would require the feature to exist). This bead ships `Unsupported`-returning stubs behind the cargo features so the env names are reserved, the config contract is stable, and the error message guides the user. ADR-0002 §3.5.

Depends on `backend-traits-define` (trait to implement) + `cargo-feature-flags` (features to gate behind).

## Subtasks

1. `src/backend/superlogical.rs` (behind `#[cfg(feature = "backend-superlogical")]`): `SuperlogicalBackend` implementing `MultiplexerBackend` with every method returning `Err(BackendError::Unsupported { backend: "superlogical", reason: "not yet released (superlogical.com beta); set FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=herdr" })`. `name()` returns `"superlogical"` (so `list_backends` can enumerate it).
2. `src/backend/tmux.rs` (behind `backend-tmux`): `TmuxBackend` stub, mirroring toron ADR-0003's "tmux returns Unsupported until un-held". Same `Unsupported` pattern; reason references toron ADR-0003.
3. `src/backend/toron_mail.rs` (behind `mail-toron`): `ToronMailBackend` implementing `MailBackend`, every method `Unsupported { backend: "toron", reason: "toron-core not yet embedded; set FLYWHEEL_MAIL=agentmail (toron ADR-0003 R1)" }`. `name()` → `"toron"`.
4. A `BackendError` enum (in `src/backend/mod.rs`): `Unsupported { backend, reason }`, `NotCompiled { feature }`, plus a passthrough `Other(anyhow::Error)`. `Display` prints actionable copy.
5. `flywheel backend list` CLI subcommand: enumerates compiled-in backends (`name + status: ready|stub`), so a user can see what's available without reading Cargo.toml.

## Approach notes

- **Stubs return errors, never panic, never silently succeed.** A stub that returns `Ok(())` would hide that the backend isn't real. `Unsupported` is the honest signal.
- The stubs exist *so the env names are reserved* — a user reading `.env.example` or AGENTS.md sees `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical` documented, sets it, and gets a clear "not yet released" message rather than a "no such backend" crash. This makes the config contract forward-stable.
- Mirror toron ADR-0003's tmux framing exactly ("returns Unsupported until un-held") so when toron-core ships its tmux impl, the semantics match.
- `BackendError::Unsupported` should include a link/hint to the relevant ADR (toron ADR-0003 / superlogical.com / this ADR-0002) in its `Display`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `FLYWHEEL_BACKEND=superlogical` (with the feature on) → every multiplexer call returns `Unsupported` with the "not yet released" message; `flywheel backend list` shows `superlogical: stub`.
- `FLYWHEEL_MAIL=toron` (feature on) → every mail call returns `Unsupported` with the "R1" message.
- With features off, the factory returns `NotCompiled` (actionable: which feature to enable).
- No stub ever returns `Ok` or panics.

## Test plan

- Unit: every stub method returns `Unsupported` (table-driven over all trait methods × all stubs).
- Unit: `flywheel backend list` output shape.
- The parity test (R0.8) excludes stubs (they can't pass parity — they're not real).

## Considerations

- Don't implement even partial superlogical/tmux/toron behavior — a half-stub is worse than a clean `Unsupported` (it implies capability that isn't there).
- When toron-core ships (R1), `ToronMailBackend` graduates from stub to real impl in-place (same file, same struct, real delegation) — the env name + feature are unchanged, so user config is stable.
- `flywheel backend list` is the user-facing discovery tool — keep its output clig.dev-disciplined (stdout=data/`--json`, stderr=messages).

## Reference
- ADR-0002 §3.5 (stubs), §11 Q1 (superlogical protocol unknown — stub must be extensible), §6 (no silent fallback).
- toron ADR-0003 §architecture layer 5 (tmux "returns Unsupported until un-held").

Committed 3f3af17 (surgical staging: 3 new stubs + factory.rs + mod.rs + beads; concurrent in-flight files untouched).

title: Respawn agents stuck in `unknown` for N consecutive polls
description:
# Respawn agents stuck in `unknown` for N consecutive polls

## Background

After `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch`, unknown agents are ignored. But a persistently unknown agent is a dead pane — the swarm is permanently down one worker and the loop never settles (unknown is not a settled state), so `--work` mode hangs forever waiting for nothing. The docs treat unknown as classification uncertainty, not proof of death; the repair must therefore wait a grace period, then act.

## Why (justification)

The skip alone trades silent loss for a hung loop. A grace period distinguishes transient classification flicker (unknown → idle → unknown) from a genuinely dead session (unknown → unknown → unknown). Once the grace elapses, respawn is the same repair the loop already uses for context exhaustion and (per `bd-send-stall-escalation`) stalled sends — one repair primitive, three triggers.

## Technical approach

- `swarm_loop` keeps `unknown_seen: HashMap<String, u64>` (workflow-local; deterministic — reconstructable from checkpointed poll results, like `assigned` at durable.rs:360).
- Each poll: status == unknown → `count += 1`; any other status → remove from map (reset).
- Pure fn `unknown_decision(status, counts, threshold=2) -> UnknownAction { None | Respawn }`: Respawn when count reaches threshold; None otherwise (and the map maintenance is done by the caller).
- On Respawn: use the SHARED respawn helper from `bd-send-stall-escalation` (one respawn path in the workflow; both triggers must funnel through it so an agent can never be double-respawned in one iteration).
- Log event `reason=unknown-stuck` with the agent name and the count.
- Threshold constant: 2 consecutive polls. At the settled interval (300s) that is ~10 min before repair; with `bd-adaptive-interval` the cadence is active while the swarm is unsettled, so the repair typically fires within ~1 min. No coupling between the beads — document the interplay only.

## Success criteria

- An agent unknown for 2+ consecutive polls is respawned; a fresh instance appears under the same name.
- An agent that flickers unknown → idle → unknown is NEVER respawned (counter resets on idle).
- Exactly one respawn per stuck agent (shared helper).

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: `unknown_decision` transitions — count 0→1→2 (Respawn at 2), reset on idle, threshold boundary (2 = respawn, 1 = wait).
- Unit: integration-style test over a fake state sequence (unknown, unknown → one Respawn; unknown, idle, unknown → zero respawns) driving the workflow's per-poll logic via the pure fns.
- Manual e2e: kill an agent process in its pane; observe skip-dispatch for 2 polls, then respawn; log evidence for `bd-e2e-hardened-loop`.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-unknown-skip-dispatch`. Uses the shared respawn helper agreed in `bd-send-stall-escalation`.

## Considerations

- Never respawn on a confirmed-working agent; the counter only advances on `unknown`.
- The threshold is a named constant, not magic: `UNKNOWN_RESPAWN_THRESHOLD: u64 = 2` with a doc comment explaining the tradeoff (transient flicker vs dead pane).
- Do not close the pane of a merely-unclassified agent — the respawn helper already splits a fresh pane BEFORE closing the old one (main.rs:2676-2686), which keeps the workspace alive; preserve that ordering.
close_reason:
Unknown-status repair implemented via the shared respawn helper. UNKNOWN_RESPAWN_THRESHOLD=2 const (doc'd tradeoff: flicker vs dead pane); pure unknown_decision(status,count,threshold) + per-poll driver track_unknown (unknown -> +1, any other status -> reset, respawn -> clean episode so exactly one respawn per stuck episode); workflow-local unknown_seen map rebuilt from checkpointed polls (deterministic replays). Respawn goes through respawn_and_requeue (now text: Option<&str> — unknown repair has nothing to requeue), logging EventKind::Respawn with reason=unknown-stuck and the count. Split-before-close pane ordering preserved.

97/97 tests (5 new: decision transitions/boundary, classified-status never fires, two-unknown sequence -> one respawn + episode reset, unknown->idle->unknown flicker -> zero respawns, per-agent independence).

E2E limitation (live-verified): on this herdr build a persistent per-agent 'unknown' status is NOT producible — SIGKILL/SIGSTOP of a running agent -> record dropped (ABSENT) in ~0.5s; freeze mid-launch -> (idle, launch_pending) then dropped; failed/timed-out agent start -> record cleaned up; the only unknown sighting is the ~0.5s launch window. Same class as bd-ojx's un-producible stalled verdict. Negative live e2e: real loop + real idle agent, queue t1..t3 -> 2 landed sends, zero respawn events, unknown branch silent. The decision->respawn wiring is unit/integration-tested per the bead's own test plan; the respawn machinery itself (respawn_and_requeue -> __respawn -> fresh pane + same-name agent) was live-proven in bd-send-stall-escalation-13b. Full live unknown e2e becomes possible once bd-read-state-fallback-zwa can classify agent state from response files (noted in handoff for that bead).

title: plan_actions: never dispatch work to `unknown` agents
description:
# plan_actions: never dispatch work to `unknown` agents

## Background

`plan_actions` (durable.rs:326-349) treats any non-working, non-blocked status as dispatchable: the catch-all arm `_ => { if !queue.is_empty() { Send } else if nudge { Nudge } else { Wait } }` covers idle, done, AND unknown. The herdr preview docs are explicit about `unknown`: "an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify its lifecycle confidently; it does not prove successful completion. Use exact `--until` states when that distinction matters."

## Why (justification)

Dispatching to an unclassified agent can deliver a prompt into a half-dead session (agent process exited, TUI crashed, detection failed, pane replaced). The queue item is consumed by an agent that may never execute it — silent loss, exactly what the epic forbids. Skipping one poll costs nothing (the loop already tolerates `Wait` actions); the swarm is only ever down one delegation, never down one queue item.

## Technical approach

- In `plan_actions` (durable.rs:326-349), match `"unknown"` EXPLICITLY → `LoopAction::Wait` (never pop the queue, never nudge). Keep the catch-all for idle/done.
- Update the fn doc comment to state the contract: unknown is not dispatchable, by design.
- Add a regression test: an unknown agent does NOT count toward "all settled" — the completion guard (durable.rs:540-546) already only matches `idle | done`, so an unknown agent keeps the loop alive. Assert it.

## Success criteria

- Unknown agents never receive queue items or nudges.
- Queue integrity: an unknown agent never consumes queue items.
- Unknown agent keeps the loop alive (completion guard regression test).

## Test plan (TDD — RED first)

- Unit: `unknown_agent_keeps_queue` — states=[unknown], queue=[p1] → queue still len 1, action is Wait.
- Unit: `unknown_with_nudge_no_send` — states=[unknown], queue=[], nudge=Some → Wait, no Nudge action.
- Unit: `unknown_not_settled` — states=[unknown], empty queue → `all_settled` false (loop does not complete).
- Manual: kill an agent process in its pane (status becomes unknown); poll with a non-empty queue → queue intact on the next poll.

## Considerations

- This bead is the SKIP half. The repair half (respawn after N consecutive unknowns) is `bd-unknown-respawn`.
- Do not conflate `done` with `unknown`: `done` is "idle after background work" (docs) and remains dispatchable.
- Interaction with `bd-adaptive-interval`: an unknown agent keeps the loop from settling, so the loop stays on the active cadence while a repair may be pending — correct and desirable.

## Project fit

"Never feed work to a session you cannot trust" — the second pillar of the epic's no-silent-loss guarantee.
close_reason: plan_actions now matches unknown explicitly -> Wait (never Send/Nudge, queue intact); doc comment states contract. Completion guard extracted to pub all_settled() (idle|done only) used by the loop and testable. 61/61 tests (3 new: unknown_agent_keeps_queue, unknown_with_nudge_no_send, unknown_not_settled). RED proven by reverting to old catch-all: 2/3 tests failed. Manual e2e: killed agent process (herdr drops record on this preview build - reconfirms bd-ojx); durable loop with non-empty queue + dead agent emitted zero send events, stayed alive (Pending), queue never consumed. Loop cleanup via resonate promises cancel + flywheel kill.

title: Swarm registry write failure: panes created but list/send read an empty registry
description:
# Swarm registry write failure: panes created but list/send read an empty registry

## Problem (live e2e, 2026-08-09)

During a crew dispatch, an agent ran `flywheel spawn toron-review --oc 2 --label "ADR-0008-debate"` (wrong project name). The failure surfaced as:

```
Flywheel swarm registry write failed
(spawn made herdr panes but list/send read a registry that's empty).
Driving opencode panes directly via herdr.
```

Root cause chain (from herdr 0.8.0-preview strings + flywheel behavior):
1. herdr persists the swarm/session registry to `session.json`; on a read failure it prints `failed to read session file` / `failed to parse session file, ignoring` and starts with an EMPTY registry.
2. A spawn that created panes while the registry write/read failed leaves the panes LIVE in herdr but INVISIBLE to `flywheel list` / `send` / `status` (which query the registry).
3. flywheel does not verify post-spawn that the workspace it just created is actually visible to list/send — the spawn "succeeds", then every subsequent command sees nothing.
4. The wrong project name (`toron-review` vs `toron`) is a skills/command-usage issue — the agent invented a project; flywheel's spawn either did not validate the project dir or the error was not surfaced loudly enough.

## Fixes proposed

### A. flywheel spawn: post-spawn visibility verification (primary)
After creating the workspace + agents, verify the new workspace appears in `workspace.list` (or `agent.list`) from the same client view list/send will use. If it does NOT:
- Fail with a LOUD error naming the registry path, the workspace id, and exact recovery steps (restart herdr: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.herdr...` or `herdr restart`; or `HERDR_SESSION` path check).
- Do NOT silently succeed (current behavior). Consider a `--no-verify` escape hatch for scripts.

### B. flywheel spawn: project-dir validation BEFORE creating panes
- Validate the project dir exists (and is initialized: has .beads/ or is a git repo) BEFORE any herdr workspace/pane is created. `flywheel spawn nonexistent-project` must exit non-zero with "project dir missing: X (run: flywheel init X)" and NO side effects.
- This turns the wrong-command case into a fast, safe failure — the agent's `toron-review` mistake becomes a clear error naming the real projects available (suggest `flywheel list` / the project dirs).

### C. Label validation (the ADR-0008-debate case)
- Decide + enforce a slug convention: labels are used in workspace metadata; hyphenated/uppercase labels (ADR-0008-debate) should either be normalized (lowercase, hyphens allowed) or rejected with guidance. Document the convention in the spawn help + the flywheel skill.

### D. Skills/template hardening (the command-usage half)
- The flywheel skill + beads templates should state the spawn contract explicitly: `flywheel spawn <project> --oc N` where <project> is the DIRECTORY NAME in ~/workspace (toron, flywheel, hachiko...), never an invented name; label is optional + slug-safe. A one-line "common mistakes" note (wrong project name; --oc with space vs =; hyphenated labels).
- This is the agent-facing fix; A-C are the code guard rails that make the mistake cheap.

## Success criteria

1. `flywheel spawn nonexistent-project --oc 2` exits non-zero, creates ZERO panes, and prints a message naming the valid projects (or the init command).
2. After a spawn, `flywheel list` ALWAYS shows the new workspace, or spawn fails loudly with recovery steps (never silent success + empty registry).
3. `--label ADR-0008-debate` is either normalized to a slug or rejected with the convention explained.
4. Unit tests: spawn validation (project exists), label normalization, post-spawn visibility check (mock/real herdr).
5. e2e T2/T3 (bd-i8x) pass against this fix.
6. Full `cargo test` green; no regression on the happy-path spawn.

## Considerations

- The registry read is herdr-side (session.json). flywheel cannot fix herdr's silent-ignore, but it CAN verify what list/send will see and fail loudly — that is the contract flywheel owns.
- The post-spawn check should be cheap (one workspace.list call) and must not add a race: verify the workspace_id returned by spawn is present, not just "any workspace".
- Coordinate with bd-a7j (reply-verification) and bd-i8x (e2e confirmation) — the T2/T3 tests there are this bead's acceptance tests.
- Skills edits live outside the repo (~/.agents/skills/flywheel/SKILL.md + integrations/*.tpl) — the code guard rails are the committed deliverable; the skill note is the companion.
close_reason: A: post-spawn visibility check (workspace.list contains the exact created ws id; loud failure with herdr-restart recovery steps; --no-verify escape). B: project-dir validated before any pane (exit 1, zero panes, lists available projects). C: --label slug-normalized (ADR-0008-debate -> adr-0008-debate, warning, empty rejected) + meta fallback so project commands still resolve custom-label swarms. D: skill spawn contract note. Unit tests: slugify_label_normalizes (+ spawn_registry_roundtrip earlier). Live-verified all three code paths on scratch swarms. Suite green; clippy clean.

title: blocked status not producible via __send on this herdr build
description:
## Background

The e2e gate (bd-e2e-hardened-loop) scenario 4 drives an agent into herdr blocked (approval prompt) via __send prompts to verify the --on-blocked mail latency bound. On this build (herdr 0.7.5-preview), opencode agents auto-approve/execute ordinary prompts — none of the tested prompts (rm -rf /nonexistent, sudo -n true, etc.) produced an approval gate; the agent stayed working/idle.

## Why

The blocked-alert path (on-blocked mail within ~2x active interval) is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and wired (notify_blocked leaf), but never e2e-verified. A real blocked signal is the one herdr state this project cannot yet produce deterministically.

## Technical approach

- Try driving blocked via herdr agent send-keys into an opencode permission prompt, or a restricted-mode agent config (deny bash + request approval), or herdr's own blocked simulation if any (check herdr api schema for a state-forcing method).
- Alternatively verify the mail path end-to-end with a FAKE blocked: register the scratch project in agent-mail, then invoke __mail-blocked directly and assert delivery (the latency bound itself is already unit-covered).
close_reason: Discovery documented: herdr 0.7.5-preview cannot be driven into blocked via __send prompts (opencode auto-approves; rm/sudo prompts verified). The blocked-alert latency bound is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and the mail path is wired (notify_blocked leaf). The e2e gate (9qa) scenario 4 records this as its single FAIL with the precise reproduction; the gate script remains the runbook — when blocked becomes producible (or the __mail-blocked direct verification lands), scenario 4 flips green.

title: pi agents spawn nameless: name-based resolution fails until manual rename
description:
## Background

`flywheel spawn --pi 1` calls herdr agent.start with a name (`flywheel-<project>-pi`), but the resulting agent record frequently has NO name field (herdr's pi integration does not register the name — unlike opencode agents which carry it). Name-based resolution then fails:

- `flywheel __send <project> <name>` -> 'agent not found'
- `--to pi` / resolve_agents matching by name -> no match
- the durable loop's `agent_target` falls back to the PANE ID, which breaks `read_output`/poll_kind lookups (the pane-id name does not resolve either)

Observed live during bd-send-stall-escalation e2e: the w18 pi agent came up nameless; the loop's CONTEXT_LIMIT guard then called poll_kind with the pane-id fallback name and crashed ('__kind failed: agent w18:p1 not found'). Renaming manually (`herdr agent rename <pane> <name>`) fixes it, and sometimes a fresh spawn registers the name correctly (w19 did) — the behavior is inconsistent.

## Why

The loop targets agents by name everywhere. A nameless agent makes the swarm unusable (send/status/loop all fail or misbehave).

## Technical approach

- Investigate herdr's agent.start/name persistence for pi (possibly a herdr-side timing/registration race).
- flywheel-side hardening: after spawn, verify the name landed (agent_list by pane) and re-apply `agent rename` until it sticks (bounded retries); or make `agent_target`/lookups fall back to pane id consistently (agent_target already does — the LOOKUP side needs the same fallback).
- e2e: spawn --pi, immediately status/send — must resolve without manual rename.
close_reason:
Spawn-time naming for nameless agent integrations. herdr.rs gains agent_rename (socket method agent.rename {target, name} — verified in the protocol schema). start_agent_with_retry (main.rs): after agent_start, the retry loop's name+pane match is extended — if a record exists on OUR pane with a missing/different name (the pi integration registers nameless), apply agent.rename(pane, requested-name) and return the named record. Name-based resolution (send/loop/status/--to) now works for pi swarms without manual `herdr agent rename`. 137/137 tests (incl. the resolver's nameless-record case).

Live e2e: `flywheel spawn scratch-e2e --pi 1` -> agent came up as flywheel-scratch-e2e-pi (named) with no manual intervention; status/send resolution worked immediately. (Previously w16/w18 pi agents came up nameless and required manual renames — see the 13b session notes.)

title: wait-output-usage: use wait-output for send-receipt + stall detection
description:
# `__wait-output` leaf + documented recipe

## Background

`bd-pane-wait-output-helper` adds the client method. This bead exposes it as a hidden leaf (consistent with the `__*` leaf pattern: shell-out boundary so the blocking client never runs on the async executor, durable.rs:9-11) and documents the recipe — docs-first discipline: usage guides the design.

## Why (justification)

The primitive is only useful if reachable from automation and understood. A hidden leaf keeps the automation surface uniform (`__poll`/`__send`/`__wait-output`), and the README recipe teaches the pane-vs-agent distinction the docs emphasize.

## Technical approach

- Hidden subcommand `__wait-output <project> <agent-or-pane> <pattern> [--regex] [--timeout-ms N]`:
  - Resolve the target to a pane id (agent name → `agent.list` lookup, same as `__send` main.rs:2558-2562; or accept a raw pane id).
  - Call `pane_wait_output`; print JSON `{"matched": bool, "matched_line": ..., "pane_id": ...}`; exit 1 on timeout / agent-not-found.
- README automation section: recipe "block on a test run" — `pane run` the test watcher, then `__wait-output --regex "passed|failed"`; plus the docs' caveat: use `agent wait` when you need LIFECYCLE semantics, `__wait-output` for raw output.
- Do NOT add a new workflow-step type (`run_workflow`/`run_pipeline`, main.rs:1785-1834) in this bead — note it as a future option in a comment; avoid scope creep.

## Success criteria

- Leaf works end-to-end (match + timeout paths); README recipe present and accurate.

## Test plan (TDD)

- Unit: argv/params building pure fn (agent-name vs pane-id resolution, --regex flag, timeout) + JSON shape.
- Manual: follow the README recipe in a scratch workspace; verify match and timeout paths; log evidence.

## Dependencies

Depends on: `bd-pane-wait-output-helper`.

## Considerations

- Hidden leaf discipline: never invoke `__*` commands from interactive workflows; the durable workflow does not use this leaf yet (it is for scripts/automation) — that is fine; the recipe is the contract.
- Keep the output machine-parseable (`--json`-style single object); stderr for messages.
- The pane/agent target resolution must reuse the existing helpers (`resolve_agents`/`agent_target` in main.rs) — no duplicate lookup logic.
close_reason:
Hidden __wait-output leaf wired to the pane-wait-output helper (efq). cmd_internal_wait_output: target resolution via pure resolve_pane_id (agent name -> pane from the project's ws-filtered agent list; raw pane id accepted; unknown -> matched:false + exit 1), wait_output_mode maps --regex to herdr's regex mode (literal substring is the leaf's "match" -> client maps to "substring"), pane_wait_output call with optional timeout; stdout {"matched", "matched_line", "pane_id"} on every path, exit 0 on match, 1 on timeout/unknown (stderr messages). The 4 efq #[allow(dead_code)] markers removed (helpers now wired). No workflow-step type added — noted as a future option in a comment (scope discipline per the bead).

README "Durable backend" gains the recipe: herdr pane run a test watcher, then __wait-output --regex 'passed|failed'; caveat: __wait-output waits on raw pane OUTPUT, herdr agent wait for lifecycle semantics. Clarified that raw panes must live in the swarm's workspace (the leaf resolves the project's workspace first).

128/128 tests (6 new: resolve_pane_id name/raw/unknown, wait_output_mode, JSON shape incl. null matched_line, PaneWaitResult rendering).

Live e2e (scratch oc swarm + split pane): match on raw pane (TEST-MARKER-READY, exit 0, matched_line from the pane), timeout path (matched:false + stderr + exit 1), agent-name positive match (matched_line from the agent's pane), agent-name resolution to the right pane, unknown target (matched:false + exit 1).

title: Wake banners cite ids the toron daemon never registered (id-vocabulary drift)
description:
# Wake banners cite ids the toron daemon never registered (id-vocabulary drift)

Repro (2026-08-21, SandySparrow session, 13+ consecutive wakes):

- Banner repeatedly cited "Most recent urgent: id c43357a1… / thread 9844e931…" ([request-release] crates/toron-cli/**) against a read-empty inbox (0 unread, 0 rows <15min old).
- The request was answered hours earlier: `toron_reply_message` with `release_decision=agreed` + `request_message_id=c43357a1…` accepted, delivery event d4172200 to TealDune confirmed.
- Re-keying the response on the thread/reservation id failed: daemon returns "no request-release message with id 9844e931… addressed to SandySparrow" — i.e. the banner's cited id was NEVER a registered request id. Only the rumor id registers.
- One wake also surfaced under the WRONG PIN (TealDune), citing TealDune's inbox row of my own reply — see bd-captain-alias-0g8a for the alias class.

Root cause hypothesis: flywheel's wake banner generation and toron's request-release state machine use different id vocabularies (reservation/thread id vs rumor event id), so a responded request can never be recognized as terminal by whatever emits the banner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every id a wake banner cites resolves through the mail surface before emission (unresolvable ids are dropped, not printed)
- [ ] A request-release that has received a release_decision response never re-fires a wake
- [ ] Contract test: respond to a synthetic request-release, assert zero subsequent wake emissions cite it

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```
close_reason:
Shipped: toron 14878ce + flywheel a5e616b.

Clause 2 (never re-fires): respond_request_release now records the responder's READ receipt on the request rumor (toron-core, best-effort after the decision DM). The bd-dbre wake filter (read rows do not wake) then drops the decided request permanently — CONTRACT TEST: synthetic request-release; pre-response the request is an unread urgent row in the holder's projection (wake candidate); post-response zero wake-citing rows remain.

Clause 1 (cited ids resolve): urgent_wake_prompt gates both citations through citable_wake_id — non-empty hex event id only. Reservation paths, thread labels, npubs, placeholders are dropped from the banner (wake still fires; no phantom reply key). Tests: unresolvable-ids-dropped (the exact repro shape: reservation-30078 / thread-9844e931), resolvable-hex-kept, id table. Existing fixtures moved to hex handles.

Gates: clippy -p flywheel --all-targets -D warnings green; clippy -p toron-core/mcp green; cargo test -p toron-core --lib green incl. new contract test; flywheel wake suite 29/0.

title: ADR-0013 Wave C remainder: resolve the profile half of 'one routing source' (decide or retire)
description:
ADR-0013 P0-5 / ADR-0032 Spec 9 remainder.

WHAT LANDED (5bdc903 code, 417c318 docs): the routing table is now the one source for a primitive's trigger — decide_trigger_for derives matchers[0] and the duplicate 32-arm match is deleted; UNROUTED_PRIMITIVES is the single 'not routed' declaration; load is loud (check_catalog, check_workflow_routes) and the decide CLI cross-checks the merged workflow catalog. See src/decide.rs and the decide_router_* tests.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN — the 'profiles' half of ADR-0013 §7's Wave C line. The table carries decide_trigger / matcher / primitive / argv / topology, but NOT the profile/role affinity a route dispatches to. RouteArgv::WorkflowRun names a workflow; the @role lives in that workflow's steps and in stages.rs seed role affinities. So 'flywheel decide' cannot say which profile a route will run as, and nothing answers 'what does this primitive run as?' in one place.

TWO ACCEPTED SHAPES — pick one, do not split the difference:
(a) ADD the affinity: a route row (or the one catalog) carries the profile role a primitive dispatches to, READ from the workflow's steps rather than re-declared, with a loud load check that the named role exists in the profile catalog. Acceptance: flywheel decide --json (and briefing) name the role and a table-wide test pins it.
(b) RETIRE the framing: ADR-0013 §7's 'profiles + workflow matchers' wording is out of scope for Spec 9, which scopes the table to flywheel-owned routing metadata and says it is not added to toron-workflow::Workflow. Write the rationale into ADR-0013 §6/§7, leave P0-5 CHANGED with the profile half explicitly out of scope, and keep verify-0013.sh green.

WHY NOT A ONE-LINER: profile.rs is a runtime-tiered catalog (compiled-ins < profiles.toml) keyed by role, while ROUTING_TABLE is a compiled constant keyed by matcher. Shape (a) must not re-introduce a second truth — the role must be derived from workflow/stage data, never re-typed into a routing row.

NOT IN SCOPE: portable ProfileDef codec (P2-11) and dead_code / profile-CLI cleanup (P2-14) — those stay their own items.
close_reason: P0-5 folded as option (a): affinity READ from workflow steps via decide::workflow_role_from_steps, gated by check_profile_routes, proven by decide_router_profile_affinity (15/15 router tests green). Commit 9f50c92. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — affinity derived from steps, never re-declared; prove-it-works — table test pins real catalog

comments.text: VERIFY caveat: that filter is shape (a)'s acceptance. Under shape (b) (retire the framing) the verify becomes `bash docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0013.sh` plus the ADR text, and this line must be updated so the bead cannot close on a test that was never written.

title: centralize workflow catalog resolution across the seven merge call sites
description:
# Context
Builtin+user(+project) merge is copy-pasted at ~7 sites (`src/main.rs` 15085/19445/25990/26164/26183, resolvers 26430/27022/27549) with INCONSISTENT tiers: some use `load()` (user tier only), some `load_layered()` (user+project). Project-tier overrides (`<project>/.flywheel/workflows/*.yaml`) apply on some paths and are silently ignored on crew-preview and two engine resolvers. A new call site can trivially pick the wrong tier or invert precedence.

# Evidence
- 26183 `all_workflows_layered` (full tiers) vs 26164 `all_workflows` (no project) vs inline merges at 15085/19445/25990.
- Resolver at 27022 uses `load_layered`; resolvers at 26430/27549 use `load()`.

# Scope
- One `resolve_workflow(name, project_root) -> Option<(Workflow, source)>` (plus one list variant); all call sites route through it; project tier flows from a single project-root source, never per-site choice.
- Delete the inline merges; keep the `MappingNote` honesty behavior byte-identical.

# Acceptance
- Tier-precedence test across all entry paths (list, run, compose-adjacent resolvers, crew preview): project > user > builtin everywhere.
- No behavior change on unshadowed names (existing suite green).

# Non-goals
- Token-expansion source fix (owned by the compose-shadow bead); this bead only unifies WHERE resolution happens.

title: doorbell afk/digest prints unbounded stale history with epoch timestamps, hiding new wakes
description: FOUND 2026-09-13 while proving bd-cak3 live. 'flywheel doorbell afk flywheel' printed 'doorbell afk digest (362 items)' consisting almost entirely of one repeated old row ('fact-miss -: fact without captain alias: [doorbell] ledger bd-test-close closed') -- and the newest ring, an Audit queued for pin QuietHeron from seconds earlier, was NOT in the output at all. The verb's own help says 'batch captain-relevant wakes since the last digest (ADR-0010 D5)', so the window is not being applied (or no durable 'last digest' watermark exists and it folds from Default every time). Separately the relative-time rendering is wrong: entries print as '[1789285824s ago]' -- a raw epoch value labelled as seconds-ago, i.e. ~56 years. Net effect: the one batch surface a human reads is unreadable noise that omits the fresh wake, so 'the operator can see why they were woken' fails even after the ring itself is correct (bd-cak3). FIX DIRECTION: persist a per-identity/workspace digest watermark and fold only rows after it; cap the batch; render ts as a real relative duration. Repro: run flywheel doorbell afk flywheel and compare against the tail of journals/doorbell-journal-<ws>.jsonl.
close_reason: Captain digest surface made readable and complete. (1) ROOT: afk folded EVERY workspace in the journal dir; the synthetic fact workspaces (manual, facts-close-*, facts-lapsed-*) have no clock-bearing Msg, so their digest drain (workspace.rs drain gated on now-last_digest_unix > interval) never fires and their whole history accumulated -- that is the 376 identical foreign rows. Now folds only the requested project's workspaces via doorbell_scoped_workspaces (shared with why, one definition). (2) TIMESTAMP: at_unix==0 means 'before any clock Msg in this fold'; now-last printed a raw epoch dressed as 's ago' (~56 years). render_digest now prints [age unknown] instead, asserted by bd_z5ut_digest_never_dresses_epoch_zero_as_an_age. (3) BOUNDED: newest --limit (default 100) with the withheld count printed -- a silently truncated digest is the same failure as an unbounded one. (4) COMPLETE: afk now also prints digest-bound wakes read from the journal rows (digest_action_entries), because the embedded fold cannot produce them (no InboxFetched arm = bd-c9jw) -- without this the surface said 'queue empty' while the operator pin's ring sat in the journal, which was the bead's exact complaint. LIVE: 376 foreign rows + fresh wake ABSENT -> 0 foreign rows, 2 real digest-bound wakes with ISO timestamps. Verify: full-suite green, clippy -D warnings clean, 2 new unit tests. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes -- the unbounded queue was a workspace-scoping bug, not a rendering one; do-not-claim-unverified -- 'age unknown' beats a number that means nothing.
